game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Three dice are rolled independently.
- Die 1 (6 faces, each equally likely): 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
- Die 2 (6 faces, each equally likely): 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
- Die 3 (6 faces, each equally likely): 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
Fair value before any reveal is 10.5, the expected sum of three dice. The standard deviation of the sum is about 2.96.

I chose the spread by weighing two effects on each side:
- **Noise traders (65%)** pay me the half-spread, but fewer of them trade as the spread widens.
- **Informed traders (35%)** only trade when the true value is beyond my quote, so I lose on those trades.

Expected profit per side for different half-spreads:

| Half-spread | Gain from noise | Loss to informed | Net |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 0.42 | 0.15 | 0.27 |
| 3 | 0.48 | 0.08 | 0.40 |
| 3.5 | 0.49 | 0.06 | 0.43 |
| 4 | 0.47 | 0.04 | 0.43 |

The best half-spread is about 3.5–4. The sum can only be a whole number, so I set the ask at 14.4. That means informed traders only buy when the sum is at least 15. The bid mirrors it at 6.6, so they only sell when the sum is at most 6.

{"bid": 6.6, "ask": 14.4}

Fair value is 10.5 (three dice at 3.5 each). The empty first quote tells us nothing, because both sides were equally far from fair.

For each ask level, I weighed what I earn from noise traders against what I lose to informed traders. The bid works the same way by symmetry.

| Ask | Expected net per quote |
|---|---|
| 12.0 | ≈ 0.15 |
| 13.0 | ≈ 0.35 |
| 14.0 | ≈ 0.43 |
| 14.4 | ≈ 0.43 |
| 15.0 | ≈ 0.42 |

Profit is flat and highest around a half-spread of 3.5 to 4.5, so I'm keeping the same quote: bid 6.6, ask 14.4.

{"bid": 6.6, "ask": 14.4}

Die 1 shows 4, so the fair value is 4 + 3.5 + 3.5 = **11**. Dice 2 and 3 still add a spread of −5 to +5 around that, with a standard deviation of about 2.4.

To choose the half-spread h, I compared what noise traders pay me against what informed traders take from me:

| h | Noise gain (0.65 × P(noise > h) × h) | Informed loss | Net per quote |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 0.84 | 0.31 | 0.53 |
| 3 | 0.97 | 0.14 | 0.83 |
| 4 | 0.95 | 0.04 | 0.91 |
| 4.5 | 0.90 | 0.02 | 0.88 |

h = 4 gives the best net. The settlement value is a whole number, and an informed trader only trades if its value is strictly above my ask or below my bid. So a 7 / 15 quote loses to informed traders only when the final sum is 16+ or 6−.

{"bid": 7.0, "ask": 15.0}

Die 1 showed 4, and the two unrevealed dice each average 3.5, so the fair value is 4 + 7 = **11**. The two remaining dice can add up to 2 through 12, so the contract settles somewhere from 6 to 16.

**Spread choice.** I compared expected profit per side of the quote for different half-spreads h. The gain comes from noise traders (65%, valuation 11 ± 4.4 normal). The cost comes from informed traders (35%), who only trade when the true value is beyond my quote.

| h | Noise gain (0.65·P·h) | Informed loss (0.35·E[(V−quote)⁺]) | Net per side |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 0.42 | 0.10 | 0.33 |
| 3 | 0.48 | 0.04 | 0.44 |
| 3.5 | 0.49 | 0.02 | 0.46 |
| 4 | 0.47 | 0.01 | 0.46 |
| 4.5 | 0.45 | 0.005 | 0.44 |

The best value is around h ≈ 3.5–4, and the curve is flat there. I'll keep a symmetric 7 / 15 quote. The position limit doesn't matter here because I start flat.

{"bid": 7.0, "ask": 15.0}

With die 1 = 4 and die 2 = 6 revealed, the fair value is 10 + 3.5 = **13.5**, and the settlement value can only be 11 to 16.

**Ask side.** If the ask is at 16 or higher, an informed trader never buys from me. So any buy there comes from a noise trader, and on average I gain the ask minus 13.5. The expected profit is 0.65 × P(noise above the ask) × (ask − 13.5):
- Ask 16.0: 0.65 × 0.285 × 2.5 ≈ 0.46
- Ask 16.5: 0.65 × 0.248 × 3.0 ≈ 0.48
- Ask 17.0: 0.65 × 0.213 × 3.5 ≈ 0.485
- Ask 17.5: 0.65 × 0.182 × 4.0 ≈ 0.47

Below 16, informed traders start buying when the value is 16, so I lose to them. The best ask is about **17.0**.

**Bid side.** The game is symmetric around 13.5, so the best bid is about **10.0**. At that price an informed trader never sells, because the value is at least 11.

Being on one side or the other has little effect on the next quote. A trade at these prices could only come from a noise trader, so it would not change the fair value.

{"bid": 10.0, "ask": 17.0}

With die 1 = 4 and die 2 = 6 revealed, the known part of the sum is 10. Die 3 is still uniform on 1 to 6, so settlement is somewhere from 11 to 16. The fair value is 13.5. The earlier no-trade outcomes tell me nothing more, because every possible value from 11 to 16 sat inside my previous 10/17 quote.

- **Informed traders:** if my ask is at least 16 and my bid at most 11, they never trade. The settlement value can't be above 16 or below 11, and they only buy strictly above my ask or sell strictly below my bid.
- **Noise traders:** their valuation is 13.5 plus noise with standard deviation 4.4. The expected edge on one side is about 0.65 × P(noise > d) × d, where d is how far my quote sits from 13.5.
  - d = 2.5 gives about 0.46.
  - d = 3.0 gives about 0.48.
  - d = 3.3 gives about 0.49, the best of these.
  - d = 3.5 gives about 0.485.
  - d = 4.0 gives about 0.47.
- **Tighter quotes:** an ask of 15 lets informed traders buy when the value is 16. That cuts the expected profit to about 0.30, so tightening doesn't pay.

The best quote is about 3.3 either side of 13.5, so bid 10.2 and ask 16.8.

{"bid": 10.2, "ask": 16.8}

game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Three dice are rolled independently.
- Die 1 (6 faces, each equally likely): 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
- Die 2 (6 faces, each equally likely): 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
- Die 3 (6 faces, each equally likely): 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
Before any dice are revealed, the fair value is 10.5, the expected sum of three dice. To set the spread, I compared, for each half-spread h, what I earn from noise traders with what I lose to informed traders on each side:

- **Earned from noise traders:** 0.65 × P(noise > h) × h, with noise standard deviation 4.4.
- **Lost to informed traders:** 0.35 × E[(V − ask)⁺], using the exact distribution of the three-dice sum.

| h | Noise gain | Informed loss | Net per side |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.0 | 0.42 | 0.16 | 0.26 |
| 3.0 | 0.48 | 0.09 | 0.40 |
| 3.5 | 0.49 | 0.06 | 0.43 |
| 4.0 | 0.47 | 0.04 | 0.43 |
| 4.5 | 0.45 | 0.02 | 0.42 |

The net profit is highest around h = 4, so I quote symmetrically 4 either side of 10.5.

{"bid": 6.5, "ask": 14.5}

Bid 5.0 / ask 13.0.

**Fair value after the trade.** Before any trades, the sum of three dice has mean 10.5. Someone sold to me at 6.5.
- An informed trader sells there only if the sum is 6 or less. That has probability 20/216 ≈ 9.3%, and the average sum in that case is 5.25.
- A noise trader sells there with probability Φ((6.5 − 10.5)/4.4) ≈ 18.2%, so 0.65 × 18.2% ≈ 11.8% overall.

Weighting the low sums by 0.35 + 0.118 and the high sums by 0.118 gives a public fair value of about 9.37.

**Expected edge per quote** (noise gain minus informed loss):

| Side | Price | Noise gain | Informed loss | Net |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ask | 11.5 | 0.43 | 0.21 | 0.22 |
| Ask | 12.5 | 0.49 | 0.13 | 0.36 |
| Ask | 13.5 | 0.47 | 0.07 | 0.40 |
| Ask | 14.0 | 0.44 | 0.04 | 0.40 |
| Bid | 6.0 | 0.49 | 0.08 | 0.41 |
| Bid | 5.5 | 0.48 | 0.05 | 0.43 |
| Bid | 5.0 | 0.46 | 0.03 | 0.43 |

The best asks are about 13.5 to 14 and the best bids about 5.0 to 5.5. Since I am already long one unit, I set the ask a little lower at 13.0 to make selling more likely. I take the bid at 5.0, the lower end, to make buying more again less likely.

{"bid": 5.0, "ask": 13.0}

Fair value now is about 13.1, so I'll quote bid 11.5 and ask 15.

1. **Revealed die.** Die 1 = 5. Dice 2 and 3 together average 7, so the starting fair value is 12.

2. **Quote 1 (they sold at 6.5).** An informed seller would need a sum of 6 or less. That is impossible now, because the sum is at least 5 + 2 = 7. So this was a noise trader and tells us nothing.

3. **Quote 2 (they bought at 13).** This trade carries information. An informed buyer needs a sum of 14 or more, which means dice 2 and 3 total 9 or more (prior probability 10/36).
   - Public fair value at that point was about 10, so a noise trader buys above 13 with probability about 0.25.
   - If dice 2 + 3 ≥ 9: chance of this trade = 0.35 + 0.65 × 0.25 ≈ 0.51.
   - If dice 2 + 3 < 9: chance of this trade = 0.65 × 0.25 ≈ 0.16.
   - Updating on this, the probability that dice 2 + 3 ≥ 9 rises to about 0.55.

4. **New expected sum.**
   - If dice 2 + 3 ≥ 9, they average 10.
   - Otherwise they average about 5.85.
   - Expected dice 2 + 3 ≈ 0.55 × 10 + 0.45 × 5.85 ≈ 8.1.
   - Fair value ≈ 5 + 8.1 ≈ 13.1.

5. **The quote.** The possible outcomes split into two clusters: totals of 7–13 or 14–17. Informed traders can hurt me on either side, so I quote fairly wide around 13.1. The ask is a little wider, since the high cluster sits further from fair value.

{"bid": 11.5, "ask": 15}

Die 1 = 5, so the settlement value is 5 + (die 2 + die 3). Before any trades, the two hidden dice average 7, which gives a fair value of 12.

**Updating on the trades**
- **Quote 1 (counterparty sold at 6.5):** With die 1 = 5, the value is at least 7, so an informed trader would never sell at 6.5. This trade was noise and tells us nothing about dice 2 and 3.
- **Quote 2 (counterparty bought at 13):** An informed trader buys here only if die 2 + die 3 ≥ 9. A noise trader buys about 18% of the time. So informed buying raises the chance of the high outcomes (likelihood about 0.53 vs 0.18).
- **Quote 3 (counterparty sold at 11.5):** An informed trader sells here only if die 2 + die 3 ≤ 6. A noise trader sells about 30% of the time. So this raises the chance of the low outcomes (likelihood about 0.65 vs 0.30).

**Result**
- Combining these gives a two-humped posterior. Roughly 45% weight is on a low sum (value 7–11) and roughly 40% on a high sum (value 14–17).
- The expected value of die 2 + die 3 is about 7.2, so fair value is about 12.2.

**Quote**
- I quote a wide spread because informed traders gain a lot on either hump.
- I'm long 1, so I shade the quote slightly downward.

{"bid": 10.0, "ask": 13.6}

With dice 1 and 2 revealed (5 + 4 = 9), the settlement value is 9 plus die 3. That puts it uniformly between 10 and 15, with a fair value of 12.5.

**How the counterparties behave**
- **Informed traders (35%)** know the exact value, which is between 10 and 15. If my ask is above 15 and my bid is below 10, they never trade and I never lose to them.
- **Noise traders (65%)** value the contract at 12.5 plus Normal noise with standard deviation 4.4.

**Expected profit on the ask side**
With the ask at 15 or higher, informed traders never buy, so profit is 0.65 × P(noise trader's valuation is above the ask) × (ask − 12.5).

| Ask | Probability a noise trader buys | Expected profit |
|---|---|---|
| 15 | 0.285 | 0.46 |
| 15.5 | 0.248 | 0.48 |
| 16 | 0.213 | 0.485 |
| 17 | 0.153 | 0.45 |

Expected profit peaks at an ask of about 16.

**Bid side**
The setup is symmetric around 12.5, so the best bid is about 9.

{"bid": 9.0, "ask": 16.0}

The contract settles at 9 + die 3, where 9 is die 1 (5) plus die 2 (4). So it will settle at a value from 10 to 15, each equally likely. The fair value is 12.5.

- **What quote 5 told us:** no one traded at 9/16. An informed trader would never trade there, because every possible value lies between 9 and 16. So the lack of a trade says nothing about die 3, and the fair value stays 12.5.
- **Informed traders:** they can only hurt me if my bid is above 10 or my ask is below 15. Quoting outside 10–15 makes them harmless.
- **Noise traders:** their valuations are 12.5 plus noise with standard deviation 4.4. For a spread distance x, the expected edge on each side is 0.65 × x × P(noise > x).
  - Checking values, x = 3.5 gives about 0.485 and x = 3.0 gives about 0.483.
  - The best point is near x ≈ 0.75 × 4.4 ≈ 3.3.
- **Quote:** a bid of 12.5 − 3.3 = 9.2 and an ask of 12.5 + 3.3 = 15.8. This puts both sides near the noise-trader optimum and outside the range where informed traders could profit.

{"bid": 9.2, "ask": 15.8}

game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Three dice are rolled independently.
- Die 1 (6 faces, each equally likely): 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
- Die 2 (6 faces, each equally likely): 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
- Die 3 (6 faces, each equally likely): 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
Before anything is revealed, the fair value is the expected sum of three dice: 3 × 3.5 = 10.5. The sum's standard deviation is about 2.96.

I picked the half-spread to maximise expected profit per side. That profit is the gain from noise traders (probability 0.65, valuation is fair value plus Normal noise with SD 3) minus the expected loss to informed traders (probability 0.35, who know the true sum).

| Ask | Noise gain | Informed loss | Net |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12.5 | ≈0.33 | ≈0.16 | ≈0.17 |
| 13.5 | ≈0.31 | ≈0.09 | ≈0.22 |
| 14.0 | ≈0.28 | ≈0.06 | ≈0.22 |
| 14.5 | ≈0.24 | ≈0.04 | ≈0.20 |

The best half-spread is about 3. By symmetry the bid goes 3 below fair value.

{"bid": 7.5, "ask": 13.5}

Before any dice are revealed, fair value is 10.5, the expected sum of three dice. The standard deviation of the sum is about 2.96. Noise traders' valuations spread around 10.5 with a standard deviation of 3, so both kinds of counterparty look roughly like a normal distribution of width 3.

**Choosing the spread:**

- **Expected profit by half-spread:** about 0.17 at 2, 0.22 at 3, 0.22 at 3.5 and 0.20 at 4. So a half-spread of roughly 3 to 3.5 does best.
- **Whole-number settlement:** The sum is always a whole number, so I put each side just short of a whole number. An ask of 13.9 is bought by an informed trader only when the sum is 14 or more, the same as an ask of 13.5. But each noise-trader sale earns 0.4 more.
- **Bid side:** By the same logic, a bid of 7.1 is hit by an informed trader only when the sum is 7 or less.
- **Result:** The quote is symmetric around 10.5, with a half-spread of 3.4.

{"bid": 7.1, "ask": 13.9}

The public fair value is still **10.5**. The sum of three fair dice has mean 10.5 and standard deviation about 2.96. The two previous quotes did not trade, which tells us almost nothing new.

I compared expected profit per side across possible quote widths. The calculation counts the gain from noise traders and the loss to informed traders, and it uses the exact distribution of the dice sum.

| Ask | Gain from noise traders (×0.65) | Loss to informed traders (×0.35) | Net expected profit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12.5 | 0.328 | 0.159 | 0.169 |
| 13.0 | 0.329 | 0.113 | 0.215 |
| 13.5 | 0.310 | 0.085 | **0.225** |
| 13.9 | 0.284 | 0.062 | 0.222 |
| 14.0 | 0.277 | 0.057 | 0.220 |

An ask of 13.5 gives the highest expected profit, and the curve is fairly flat around it. The dice sum is symmetric around 10.5, so the matching bid is 7.5.

{"bid": 7.5, "ask": 13.5}

The first die came up 1. The other two dice have an expected sum of 7, so fair value is **8**. Settlement can land anywhere from 3 to 13.

I chose the ask by trading off profit against two kinds of counterparty:
- **Noise traders:** their valuation is 8 plus noise with standard deviation 3. I earn (ask − 8) each time one buys.
- **Informed traders:** I lose whatever the true value exceeds my ask, so the expected loss is E[(V − ask)⁺].

Expected profit per quote on the ask side:

| Ask | Noise profit | Informed loss | Net |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10.0 | 0.328 | 0.097 | 0.231 |
| 10.5 | 0.329 | 0.068 | 0.261 |
| 11.0 | 0.310 | 0.039 | **0.271** |
| 11.5 | 0.277 | 0.024 | 0.253 |

An ask of about 11 does best. The bid side is symmetric around 8, so the bid is 5.

{"bid": 5.0, "ask": 11.0}

Die 1 is 1, so the sum of the two unrevealed dice is between 2 and 12 with mean 7. The public fair value is therefore 8, with a possible range of 3 to 13. The no-trade at quote 4 doesn't move this estimate meaningfully.

**Choosing the half-spread h around 8.** For each side I compared the expected gain from noise traders with the expected loss to informed traders. Noise traders have SD 3 and arrive with probability 0.65. Informed traders know the value and arrive with probability 0.35.

| h | Gain from noise traders | Loss to informed traders | Net per side |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.0 | 0.33 | 0.10 | 0.23 |
| 2.5 | 0.33 | 0.07 | 0.26 |
| 3.0 | 0.31 | 0.04 | 0.27 |
| 3.5 | 0.28 | 0.02 | 0.25 |

A half-spread of about 3 is close to optimal. I'll quote symmetrically around 8.

{"bid": 5.0, "ask": 11.0}

Fair value is 8: die 1 shows 1, and the two unrevealed dice average 7. Their sum runs from 2 to 12 with a standard deviation of about 2.4.

I compared the expected profit per quote at different ask prices. Each figure is the gain from noise traders minus the loss to informed traders:
- Ask 9.5: about +0.16
- Ask 10.5: about +0.26
- Ask 11.0: about +0.27, roughly the best

The bid side is symmetric around 8, so the best bid is about 5. The quote stays at 5 / 11.

{"bid": 5, "ask": 11}

Dice 1 and 2 sum to 7, so the contract settles between 8 and 13, with a fair value of 10.5.

**Informed traders:** they trade only if the true value is strictly beyond my price. At an ask of 13.0 no informed trader buys, since the most the contract can be worth is 13. At a bid of 8.0 no informed trader sells, since the least it can be worth is 8.

**Noise traders:** their valuation is 10.5 plus noise with standard deviation 3. At an ask of 13.0, about 20% of them buy and I earn 2.5 on each trade. That gives an expected profit of about 0.65 × 0.20 × 2.5 ≈ 0.33 per side, which is about the best on a grid of asks from 12.5 to 13.5. The bid works the same way in reverse.

{"bid": 8.0, "ask": 13.0}

Fair value is 10.5. The revealed dice sum to 1 + 6 = 7, and die 3 averages 3.5, so settlement is uniform on 8 to 13.

**Ask.** For each ask level, the expected profit is:
- 0.35 × P(true value > ask) × (ask − value), which is the loss to informed buyers;
- plus 0.65 × P(noise valuation > ask) × (ask − 10.5), where the noise valuation is 10.5 + N(0, 3).

| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 12.0 | ≈ 0.24 |
| 12.5 | ≈ 0.30 |
| 13.0 | ≈ 0.33 |
| 13.5 | ≈ 0.31 |

At 13 or above, no informed trader can buy at a loss to me, because the maximum settlement is 13. An ask of 13 is about optimal.

**Bid.** The bid works the same way in reverse, so the best bid is 8.

The no-trade at quote 7 does not move fair value. That quote was symmetric around 10.5, so a no-trade tells me nothing about the direction.

{"bid": 8, "ask": 13}

Dice 1 and 2 are revealed, so the known sum is 1 + 6 = 7. Die 3 is still hidden and uniform on 1 to 6, so the settlement value is somewhere from 8 to 13. Its expected value is 10.5. No trades have happened, so the public fair value stays 10.5.

**Ask:**
- On noise traders alone, the expected profit per quote, (a − 10.5) × P(noise valuation > a), peaks at an ask near 12.75.
- Any ask below 13 can be hit by an informed trader when the true value is 13, which loses money.
- Expected profit at a few asks:

| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 12.0 | about 0.24 |
| 12.5 | about 0.30 |
| 12.9 | about 0.325 |
| 13.0 | about 0.329 |

- 13.0 is best: no informed trader buys there, and almost no noise profit is lost compared with 12.75.

**Bid:** The problem is symmetric around 10.5, so the best bid is 8.0.

{"bid": 8.0, "ask": 13.0}

game.description:

game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
Before anything is revealed, the fair value is 10.5, the expected sum of three dice. The settlement value has a standard deviation of about 2.96.

I compared half-spreads using a normal approximation for both trader types:
- **Noise traders:** I earn the half-spread whenever their valuation falls outside my quotes.
- **Informed traders:** I lose by the expected amount the true value lies beyond my quote.

| Half-spread | Expected net profit per quote |
|---|---|
| 1.5 | +0.20 |
| 2.0 | +0.35 |
| 2.5 | +0.43 |
| 3.0 | +0.45 |
| 3.5 | +0.43 |

A half-spread of 3 does best, so I quote 7.5 / 13.5 around the fair value of 10.5.

{"bid": 7.5, "ask": 13.5}

Fair value is 10.5 (three fair dice), and the sum has a standard deviation of about 2.96. Last quote's no-trade doesn't move it. I compared expected profit per side at different half-spreads, as noise-trader spread capture minus losses to informed traders:

| Half-spread | Expected profit per side |
|---|---|
| 2.0 | 0.17 |
| 2.5 | 0.22 |
| 3.0 | 0.225 |
| 3.5 | 0.22 |

Profit peaks around a half-spread of 3, so I'll quote close to that, slightly tighter than last time.

{"bid": 7.6, "ask": 13.4}

The 13.4 buy moved my fair-value estimate up to about 11.9–12.0, so I'm centring the quote there instead of at 10.5.

**Prior.** The sum of three dice has mean 10.5 and standard deviation of about 2.96. Nothing has been revealed yet.

**What the buy at 13.4 tells me:**
- An informed trader buys only if the sum is 14 or more. That has probability 35/216, about 0.162.
- A noise trader buys if 10.5 plus Normal noise (sd 3) exceeds 13.4. That has probability about 0.167.
- So the buy is only mildly informative about direction, but it weights the high tail. Given a sum of 14 or more, the expected sum is 15.
- Combining both cases, the expected sum given a buy is about 12.0.
- The earlier no-trade at 7.5/13.5 points slightly towards the middle. Fair value is therefore about 11.9–12.0.

**Quote.** I'm keeping a fairly wide spread around 11.9 to protect against informed traders (35% chance). I'm short 1, so I lean slightly up.

{"bid": 9.5, "ask": 14.3}

Fair value given die 1 = 4, updated for the trade history, is about 12.3, so I'm quoting roughly ±2 around it.

- **Without history:** with die 1 = 4 and two unseen dice averaging 7, the sum would be worth 11.
- **Quote 2:** someone bought from me at 13.4. An informed trader only does that if the sum is 14 or more, meaning the two unseen dice total at least 10.
- **Quote 3:** nobody traded at 9.5 / 14.3. An informed trader stays out only if the sum is between 10 and 14. This counts against the extreme outcomes.
- **Updated estimate:** weighting each possible total of the two unseen dice by how likely it makes these two observations, their expected total comes to about 8.3. That puts fair value near 12.3.
- **Spread:** informed traders know the exact value, so a spread of about ±2 protects against them. It still sits inside the range where noise traders, whose valuations vary by about 3 around fair, will often trade with me.

{"bid": 10.3, "ask": 14.3}

Die 1 is 4, so the settlement is 4 plus the sum of two dice (X). With no other information, fair value would be 11.

The trading history moves that up. I updated on each step as a Bayesian, assuming informed traders trade when the true value is outside my quote:
- **Quote 2:** someone bought at 13.4. That favours a final sum of 14 or more.
- **Quotes 3 and 4:** no one traded. That makes extreme outcomes less likely, especially sums of 15–16.

Combined, these give E[X] ≈ 8.5, so public fair value is about 12.5. The single most likely sum is 14 (X = 10).

**Ask:** I set it just above 14 so informed traders holding a 14 don't lift me.

**Bid:** I set it around 10.8. Informed traders only sell there when the sum is 10 or less, which now looks unlikely.

The quote is fairly wide around 12.5, which still catches noise traders on both sides.

{"bid": 10.8, "ask": 14.2}

Die 1 = 4 and the other two dice average 7, so the prior fair value is 11. Two buys at my ask (13.4 and 14.2) push the expected total up. The no-trade quotes at 10.3/14.3 and 9.5/14.3 cap how far it rises.

- **Fair value:** Weighting each possible die 2 + die 3 total by how likely the five past outcomes were under informed and noise traders gives about 8.7. That puts the expected settlement near 12.7.
- **Ask:** The informed traders who still buy here are the ones who know the total is 15 or more, so the ask stays wide at 14.6.
- **Bid:** I am short 2, so I skew slightly upward and set the bid at 11.2, a bit closer to fair than the ask.

{"bid": 11.2, "ask": 14.6}

The contract is worth 8 plus die 3. My estimate of fair value is about 11.6, and I quote 9.0 / 14.0.

**Fair value.** Die 1 and die 2 are both 4, so settlement is 9 to 14. With no other information the expected value is 11.5. Past trades shift this slightly, depending on whether each could have come from an informed trader.

- The four no-trade quotes do carry information. An informed trader would have traded at some of them for certain die 3 values, so no trade makes those values less likely:
  - Quote 1 (8 / 13) counts against die 3 = 6.
  - Quote 3 (7.3 / 12) counts against die 3 = 5 or 6.
  - Quote 4 (10.4 / 15.4) counts against die 3 = 1 or 2.
  - Quote 6 (11.3 / 15.9) counts against die 3 = 1, 2 or 3.
- Combining these, the expected value of die 3 is about 3.6, so the expected settlement is about 11.6.

**Choosing the quote.**
- **Ask at 14.0:** an informed trader never buys, because the value cannot exceed 14. A noise trader buys about 21% of the time, earning roughly 2.4 per trade.
- **Bid at 9.0:** an informed trader never sells, because the value cannot be below 9. A noise trader sells about 19% of the time, earning roughly 2.6 per trade.
- Tighter quotes, such as an ask of 13.0–13.5 or a bid of 9.5, start trading with informed counterparties. That loss outweighs the extra noise trades.

My position is -1, so both sides can be quoted within the ±5 limit.

{"bid": 9.0, "ask": 14.0}

**Quote 9: bid 9.0, ask 14.0.**

Dice 1 and 2 total 6 + 2 = 8, and die 3 is uniform on 1–6. So the contract settles somewhere from 9 to 14, with expected value 11.5.

**The stage-3 trades tell us nothing about the value.**
- In quote 7 someone bought at 14. An informed trader buys only if the value is above 14, which cannot happen, so this was noise.
- In quote 8 someone sold at 9. An informed trader sells only if the value is below 9, which also cannot happen, so this was noise too.
- Public fair value therefore stays at about 11.5.

**Choosing the ask** (expected profit per quote, with noise valuations ~ N(11.5, 3)):

| Ask | Profit from noise buyers | Expected loss to informed | Net |
|---|---|---|---|
| 14.0 | 0.8 × 0.202 × 2.5 ≈ 0.405 | 0 | ≈ 0.405 |
| 13.9 | ≈ 0.407 | ≈ 0.003 | ≈ 0.404 |
| 14.2 | — | 0 | ≈ 0.397 |
| 14.5 | — | 0 | ≈ 0.381 |
| 12.9 | — | ≈ 0.04 | ≈ 0.32 |

An ask of 14.0 is optimal. Informed traders never buy there, because the value cannot exceed 14. The bid is symmetric at 9.0.

{"bid": 9.0, "ask": 14.0}

game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Three dice are rolled independently.
- Die 1 (6 faces, each equally likely): 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
- Die 2 (6 faces, each equally likely): 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
- Die 3 (6 faces, each equally likely): 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
Fair value is 10.5 (three dice average 3.5 each). I'm choosing a symmetric spread by trading off two things. Wider quotes make more on each noise trade but trade less often. Narrower quotes trade more but lose more to informed traders.

**Expected profit per side as the half-spread h changes:**
- **h = 1.5 (ask 12.0):** noise trades earn about 0.370. Informed trades lose about 0.117. Net about 0.253.
- **h = 2.0 (ask 12.5):** noise trades earn about 0.404. Informed trades lose about 0.091. Net about 0.313.
- **h = 2.5 (ask 13.0):** noise trades earn about 0.405. Informed trades lose about 0.065. Net about 0.340.
- **h = 2.9 (ask 13.4):** noise trades earn about 0.387. Informed trades lose about 0.052. Net about 0.335.

A half-spread of about 2.5 does best, so I quote 8.0 / 13.0.

{"bid": 8.0, "ask": 13.0}

A sell at my bid of 8 is weak evidence that the sum is low, so I'm moving my fair value down from 10.5 to about 9.75.

**How I got 9.75**
- Before any trading, the expected sum of three dice is 10.5.
- A noise trader sells below 8 with probability about 0.20, since 8 is about 0.83 standard deviations below 10.5.
- An informed trader sells only if the sum is 7 or less. That has probability 35/216 ≈ 0.16, and the average sum in those cases is 6.
- The chance of seeing a sell at all is 0.8×0.20 + 0.2×0.16 ≈ 0.192.
- Combining these, the expected sum given a sell is (0.16×10.5 + 0.0324×6) / 0.192 ≈ 9.74.

**My quote**
- I centre my quote slightly below 9.75 because I am already long one unit.
- I keep the spread fairly wide to protect against informed traders, since nothing has been revealed yet.

{"bid": 8.4, "ask": 11.0}

The fair value estimate is about 9.8, slightly below the prior of 10.5.

- **Prior:** Three dice average 10.5, with a standard deviation of about 2.96.
- **Quote 1 (sold to me at 8):** About 30% of the chance now sits on an informed seller, meaning the sum is 7 or less (average 6). The other 70% is a noise seller, with a sum averaging about 11.4. Together that gives about 9.75.
- **Quote 2 (no trade at 8.4 / 11):** No trade is somewhat more likely when the sum is 9 to 11. That nudges the estimate back up a little, to about 9.8.

I'm long 1 and want a spread wide enough to cover the 20% informed traders. I'll centre the quote slightly below fair value (about 9.7) so a sale to reduce my position is a bit more likely than another buy.

{"bid": 8.3, "ask": 11.1}

Die 1 = 5, so before any trading the expected sum is 5 + 7 = 12.

**Reading the last trade.** Someone sold to me at 10.3, so I weigh who that seller likely was:
- **Informed seller:** they sell only if the sum is 10 or less, which means die 2 + die 3 ≤ 5. That has probability 10/36. Weighted by the 0.2 chance of an informed trader, this gives about 0.056.
- **Noise seller:** they sell if 12 + noise < 10.3. That has probability Φ(−0.57) ≈ 0.285. Weighted by 0.8, this gives about 0.228.
- **Chance the seller was informed:** 0.056 / (0.056 + 0.228) ≈ 0.2. If informed, the expected sum is about 9. If noise, it stays at 12.

**Fair value.** The updated estimate is about 0.2 × 9 + 0.8 × 12 ≈ 11.4.

**Quote.** I'm already long 2, so I shift both prices slightly downward to make selling more likely than buying. I keep a reasonable spread to protect against informed traders.

{"bid": 9.8, "ask": 12.4}

Die 1 is 5, so before trading the fair value was 5 + 7 = 12. The stage-2 trading lowers that to about 11.3:

- **Quote 4:** a counterparty sold to me at 10.3. That fits an informed trader holding a low die 2 + die 3 total. A noise trader would sell there only about 28% of the time.
- **Quote 5:** nobody traded at 9.8 / 12.4. That fits a settlement value of 10, 11 or 12 (die 2 + die 3 of 5, 6 or 7).

Putting both into Bayes' rule gives an expected die 2 + die 3 of about 6.3, so the fair value is about 11.3.

I'm long 2, so I centre my quotes slightly low to make selling more likely. The spread is about ±1.4 around fair value. That guards against informed traders while still trading with noise traders, whose valuations vary with standard deviation 3.

{"bid": 9.6, "ask": 12.3}

Dice 1 and 2 are known: 5 + 6 = 11. Die 3 is uniform on 1–6, so settlement is uniform on 12–17 with a fair value of 14.5. There has been no trading yet this stage, so the public fair value is still 14.5.

**Choosing the ask.** I compared expected profit per quote for several asks:

| Ask | Profit from noise traders | Loss to informed traders | Net |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | 0.37 | −0.03 | 0.34 |
| 16.5 | 0.40 | −0.02 | 0.39 |
| 17 | 0.405 | 0 | **0.405** |
| 17.5 | 0.38 | 0 | 0.38 |

An ask of 17 loses nothing to informed traders, because the settlement value can never exceed 17. That makes it optimal.

**Choosing the bid.** The bid works the same way in reverse. A bid of 12 is never below the settlement value, so informed traders cannot profit from selling to me. It earns the same expected profit as the ask.

**Position.** I am long 1, which is well inside the ±5 limit. Since I only care about expected profit, I don't need to skew the quotes.

{"bid": 12.0, "ask": 17.0}

Dice 1 and 2 are revealed as 5 and 6, so the sum is 11 plus die 3. Die 3 is uniform on 1 to 6, so settlement is uniform on 12 to 17 with fair value 14.5. The quote 7 history tells us nothing about die 3, since no trade happened at 12 / 17 and every possible value lies in that range.

**Bid side.** Noise traders value the contract at 14.5 + N(0, 3). An informed trader sells only if the true value is below my bid. Expected profit for each bid:

| Bid | Noise sells (prob.) | Noise profit (0.8 × prob. × edge) | Informed loss | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 13.0 | 0.31 | 0.370 | −0.033 | 0.337 |
| 12.5 | 0.25 | 0.404 | −0.017 | 0.387 |
| 12.2 | 0.22 | 0.408 | −0.007 | 0.401 |
| **12.0** | 0.20 | 0.405 | 0 | **0.405** |
| 11.8 | 0.18 | 0.397 | 0 | 0.397 |

A bid of 12.0 is best. Informed traders never sell there, because no settlement value is below 12.

**Ask side.** The problem is symmetric around 14.5, so the best ask is 17.0, where informed traders never buy.

My position of +1 is far from the ±5 limits, so inventory doesn't change the quote.

{"bid": 12.0, "ask": 17.0}

Dice 1 and 2 are revealed (5 + 6 = 11), so settlement is 11 + die 3, which can be 12 to 17. The public fair value is 14.5.

The buy at 17 on quote 8 must have come from a noise trader. An informed trader buys only if the value is above the ask, and the value cannot exceed 17. So that trade tells us nothing about die 3.

On the ask side, at an ask of 17 the informed trader can never profitably buy. Noise traders, with valuations around 14.5 plus or minus 3, buy about 20% of the time. That earns 2.5 per trade, roughly 0.40 expected from the noise side.

Moving the ask in a little, to 16.8 or 16.9, gives about the same expected profit. It loses a little when die 3 shows 6, so nothing clearly beats 17.

The bid side is symmetric, so I bid at 12, the lowest possible settlement. With position 0, there is no inventory reason to skew either side.

{"bid": 12, "ask": 17}

game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Three dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (4 faces, each equally likely): 0, 1, 4, 10.
- Die 2 (8 faces, each equally likely): 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 4, 4, 9.
- Die 3 (8 faces, each equally likely): 0, 2, 7, 7, 8, 8, 9, 9.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
The expected settlement value is the sum of the three die means:

- **Die 1:** (0 + 1 + 4 + 10) / 4 = 3.75
- **Die 2:** (0 + 0 + 0 + 1 + 2 + 4 + 4 + 9) / 8 = 2.5
- **Die 3:** (0 + 2 + 7 + 7 + 8 + 8 + 9 + 9) / 8 = 6.25

So the fair value is 12.5.

The variances are about 15.2, 8.5 and 9.9. That gives a total variance of about 33.6, so the settlement value has a standard deviation of about 5.8. This matches the noise traders' spread.

**Choosing the spread width:**
- Half of counterparties are informed, so a tight quote mostly loses to them.
- Assume the value is roughly normal with the same spread as the noise traders. Write the half-spread as z standard deviations.
- Expected profit is then proportional to z·(1−Φ(z)) − φ(z)/2.
- This peaks at about z ≈ 1.2, which is a half-spread of about 6.5–7.

I quote 6.0 / 19.0, centred near 12.5.

{"bid": 6.0, "ask": 19.0}

The prior expected sum is 3.75 + 2.5 + 6.25 = 12.5.

**Updating on the sell at 6**
- An informed trader sells at 6 only if the sum is below 6. That happens with probability 28/256 ≈ 0.11, and the average sum in those cases is about 2.75.
- A noise trader sells at 6 with probability about 0.13. That trade says nothing about the value, so the expected sum stays at 12.5 in that case.
- Weighting the two cases, the chance the seller was informed is about 0.45.
- The updated fair value is about 0.45 × 2.75 + 0.55 × 12.5 ≈ 8.1.

**Quote**
- I keep a wide spread because half the counterparties are informed and the value distribution has long tails.
- I am already long 1, so I shade the quote slightly lower to make selling a bit more likely than buying.

{"bid": 5, "ask": 11}

No dice have been revealed yet, so I start from the prior. The expected values are 3.75 for die 1, 2.5 for die 2 and 6.25 for die 3. That puts the expected sum at 12.5, with a standard deviation of about 5.8.

The two trades so far point in opposite directions. Someone sold at 6, which hints the value is low. Someone bought at 11, which hints the value is above 11. Together they roughly cancel, so I keep fair value near 12.

I'm flat, so I quote roughly symmetrically around 12. The spread is wide to protect against informed traders, but tight enough that noise traders still trade.

{"bid": 8.5, "ask": 15.5}

With die 1 = 0, the settlement is die 2 plus die 3. The trading so far splits the likely outcomes into two clusters, with a fair value of about 9.

**Possible sums.** Die 2 + die 3 is either:
- a low cluster of 0–4, or
- a middle range of 6–13, or
- a high cluster of 16–18 (only when die 2 = 9).

**What the stage‑1 trades tell me.** Each trade could come from an informed or a noise trader.
- The sale to my bid at 6 points to a low sum.
- The purchases from my asks at 11 and 15.5 point to a high sum.
- These conflict, so at least one counterparty was a noise trader.

**Posterior.** Weighting each sum by its prior and the likelihood of those three trades gives:
- about 42% on the low cluster (average around 2);
- about 25% on the 6–13 range;
- about 33% on the 16–18 cluster.

The posterior mean is about 9, which is the public fair value.

**Choosing the quotes.** I compared, at each price, the loss to informed traders against the gain from noise traders (fair value 9, noise SD 5.8).
- **Ask:** At 14 or lower, informed buyers holding a high sum cost about as much as noise buyers pay me. At 16, an informed buyer gains at most 2, and noise buyers (about 11% chance of trading) pay a large premium. Expected gain is about +0.29 per quote.
- **Bid:** A bid of 1.5 can only be hit by informed sellers when the sum is 0 or 1. Noise sellers (about 10%) sell to me far below fair value. Expected gain is about +0.28 per quote.

{"bid": 1.5, "ask": 16}

Die 1 = 0, so settlement is die 2 + die 3. On the prior alone that has a mean of 8.75.

**Posterior after the trade history.** I updated each possible value of die 2 + die 3 on the four earlier quotes.
- The sale at 6 points to a low settlement.
- The buys at 11 and 15.5 point to a high one.
- The no-trade at 1.5/16 adds a little.

The result is two-peaked:
- about 42% chance the settlement is at most 4;
- about 31% chance it is between 6 and 13;
- about 27% chance it is between 16 and 18.

The public fair value is about 8.7.

**Choosing each side.** A noise trader is worth (my edge versus fair value) × (chance it trades), weighted by 0.5. An informed trader costs its expected gain at my price, also weighted by 0.5.

| Side | Price | Gain from noise | Loss to informed | Net |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ask | 12 | +0.47 | −0.66 | −0.19 |
| Ask | 15 | +0.44 | −0.23 | +0.20 |
| Ask | 16 to 17 | | | about +0.28 |
| Bid | 5 | +0.48 | −0.55 | −0.07 |
| Bid | 2.5 | +0.44 | −0.13 | +0.31 |
| Bid | 1.9 | +0.41 | −0.06 | +0.35 |

Asks of 12 or below and bids of 5 or above lose money because so much probability sits at the two ends. I'll quote a wide spread around the two clusters: bid 1.9, ask 16.5.

{"bid": 1.9, "ask": 16.5}

Die 1 = 0, so the settlement value is S = die 2 + die 3, which can be at most 18.

**Prior.** Die 2 averages 2.5 and die 3 averages 6.25, so before any trading the expected sum is 8.75.

**What the trades tell me.** I scored each possible S by how likely the trades so far would be, with half the counterparties informed and half noise.
- **Quote 4:** at ask 16 no trade happened. An informed trader would have bought if S were 17 or 18, so this pulls weight away from those values.
- **Quote 5:** someone bought at 16.5. An informed trader only does that if S is 17 or 18. A noise trader does it only about 9% of the time.
- **Stage 1:** there were buys at 11 and 15.5, which also point to a high sum. The sell at 6 points the other way.

**Posterior.** The probability of S being 17 or 18 comes out at about 0.59. There is also a smaller cluster at S between 2 and 5, with probability about 0.17. The posterior mean is about 13, so the distribution has two humps and is uncertain.

**Quote.**
- **Bid around 7:** at roughly this level, losses to informed sellers when S is low about match the gains from noise sellers.
- **Ask around 17.2:** an informed buyer only takes this when S = 18, and loses me little. Noise buyers who pay above the roughly 13 fair value give a positive expected edge.

These levels depend on my guess for the public fair value, which is uncertain.

{"bid": 7, "ask": 17.2}

Die 1 is 0 and die 3 is 9, so the settlement is 9 plus die 2. Die 2 averages 20/8 = 2.5, so the public fair value is about 11.5. The possible settlement values are 9 (prob 3/8), 10, 11, 13, 13 and 18.

**Ask side:**
- An informed buyer only lifts an ask in the 13–18 range when the value is 18.
- Expected edge per quote is about 0.29 at an ask of 15, 0.41 at 17 and 0.43 at 18.
- I'll ask 18. At that price the informed buyer can never make money off me, and I still get some noise buyers.

**Bid side:**
- Informed traders sell whenever the value is below my bid. That happens with probability 5/8 (values 9, 10 or 11) for a bid between 11 and 13, which earns me good spread.
- Noise sellers above 11.5 cost me a little.
- Expected edge is about 0.62 at bids of 12–12.5, better than about 0.49 for a low bid near 7.
- Buying also moves my -2 position toward flat, so I'll bid 12.4.

{"bid": 12.4, "ask": 18}

Settlement is 9 plus die 2. Inferring die 2 from the trading history, my rough estimate is about 15.9, and the most likely value is 18 (about 68%).

**What is known.** Die 1 = 0 and die 3 = 9, so settlement = 9 + die 2. The possible values are 9, 9, 9, 10, 11, 13, 13 and 18, each equally likely before looking at trades.

**What the trades suggest (rough Bayesian estimate).**
- **Quote 7 (buy at 18):** settlement cannot exceed 18, so an informed trader would never buy there. This trade tells us nothing about die 2.
- **Stage 2:** there was no trade at 16, a buy at 16.5, and no trade at 17.2. Together these favour die 2 = 9 (value 18) by about 2 to 1.
- **Stage 1:** there were buys at 11 and at 15.5. These also favour high values, especially 18.
- **Rough posterior:**

| Value | Probability |
|---|---|
| 9 | 0.09 |
| 10 | 0.03 |
| 11 | 0.03 |
| 13 | 0.17 |
| 18 | 0.68 |

**Bid.** If I buy at a bid, an informed trader only sells when the value is below it. Those cases are mostly 9 to 11, which have low probability. A noise trader sells with no information, so on average I pay below a value of about 15.9. Expected profit peaks around 0.4 for bids of roughly 9.5 to 10. Buying also reduces my short position.

**Ask.** At any ask of 18 or more, an informed trader never buys. Only noise traders buy, and each sale earns about the ask minus 15.9. Expected profit is about 0.49 at an ask near 20, which is the highest of the asks I checked.

{"bid": 10, "ask": 20}

Bid 8.0, ask 18.0. Each side earns about +0.47 to +0.49 in expected profit.

**Settlement value.** Die 1 = 0 and die 3 = 9, so settlement is 9 + die 2. Die 2's faces give possible values of 9, 9, 9, 10, 11, 13, 13 and 18.

**What the stage-3 trades tell us.**
- **Quote 7:** someone bought at 18. An informed trader buys only if the value is strictly above 18, which is impossible. So this was a noise trader, and it says nothing about die 2.
- **Quote 8:** nobody traded at 10 / 20. An informed trader would have sold at 10 if the value were 9. The no-trade therefore makes a value of 9 less likely.
  - Before this quote the public fair value was about 11.5. A noise trader would not trade at these prices with probability about 0.53.
  - The chance of seeing no trade is 0.27 if the value is 9 and 0.77 for every other value.
  - Updated probabilities: 9 ≈ 0.17, 10 ≈ 0.17, 11 ≈ 0.17, 13 ≈ 0.33, 18 ≈ 0.17.
  - Updated fair value ≈ 12.3.

**Ask.** At 18 or above, no informed trader buys, because the highest possible value is 18. Expected profit from noise buyers:

| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 17 | 0.41 (includes the informed loss when the value is 18) |
| 18 | 0.47 |
| 18.5 | 0.44 |
| 19 | 0.42 |

So I set the ask at 18.0.

**Bid.** At 9 or below, no informed trader sells, because the lowest possible value is 9. Expected profit from noise sellers:

| Bid | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 7 | 0.48 |
| 8 | 0.49 |
| 9 | 0.47 |
| 10 | 0.31 (includes the informed loss when the value is 9) |

So I set the bid at 8.0.

{"bid": 8.0, "ask": 18.0}

game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Three dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (4 faces, each equally likely): 0, 1, 4, 10.
- Die 2 (8 faces, each equally likely): 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 4, 4, 9.
- Die 3 (8 faces, each equally likely): 0, 2, 7, 7, 8, 8, 9, 9.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
Expected settlement is 3.75 + 2.5 + 6.25 = 12.5, and its standard deviation is about 5.8. With half the counterparties informed, I'm using a fairly wide symmetric spread of about ±7 around 12.5.

{"bid": 5.5, "ask": 19.5}

The first trade was a buy at 19.5, which is a signal that the sum may be high.

**Prior fair value.** The die means are 3.75, 2.5 and 6.25, so the prior expected sum is 12.5.

**How likely is a buy at 19.5 from each type?**
- An informed buyer needs the sum to be above 19.5. That happens with probability about 31/256 ≈ 0.12.
  - Die 1 = 10 needs dice 2 and 3 to total at least 10: probability 25/64.
  - Die 1 = 4 needs dice 2 and 3 to total at least 16: probability 6/64.
  - Die 1 = 0 or 1 cannot get there.
- A noise buyer needs a valuation above 19.5 from 12.5 plus noise with standard deviation 5.8. That is P(Z > 1.21) ≈ 0.11.

**Updating on the buy.** The chance the buyer was informed rises to about 0.515. If informed, the expected sum given it exceeds 19.5 is about 22.4. If it was noise, the fair value stays 12.5. The updated fair value is 0.515 × 22.4 + 0.485 × 12.5 ≈ 17.6.

**Quote.** The value is now quite uncertain: it is either high (around 22) or near the prior. I'll quote a wide market around 17.6 to limit losses to informed traders, while still trading with noise traders.

{"bid": 14.0, "ask": 21.0}

Fair value is about 18, so I quote 15 / 22, roughly symmetric around it.

**Prior.** The dice means are 3.75, 2.5 and 6.25, so the expected sum is 12.5.

**Quote 1: someone bought at 19.5.**
- An informed trader buys there only if the sum is 20 or more. That has probability 31/256, about 0.121, and those outcomes average about 22.4.
- A noise trader values the contract at 12.5 plus noise, so it buys above 19.5 with probability about 0.113.
- The two explanations are about equally likely, so the fair value moves to about 17.6.

**Quote 2: no trade at 14 / 21.**
- If the counterparty was informed, the sum is between 14 and 21.
- If it was noise, its valuation is about 17.6 plus noise. That lands between 14 and 21 with probability about 0.45.
- This rules out mainly the very high and very low sums. My rough estimate of the fair value is now about 18.

**Quote 3.** I keep a wide spread because half the counterparties know the exact sum and the possible sums range from 0 to 28. I quote 15 / 22 around the estimate of 18. I am short 1, but that is small enough that I don't skew the quote for it.

{"bid": 15, "ask": 22}

Die 1 = 10 is revealed, so the value is 10 plus dice 2 and 3. Without the trading history, the expected value of dice 2 and 3 is 2.5 + 6.25 = 8.75, giving a fair value of 18.75.

**What the history adds:**
- At quote 1, someone bought at 19.5. An informed counterparty only does that if the value is above 19.5. A noise trader does it only about 11% of the time.
- At quotes 2 and 3 there was no trade. Informed counterparties would have stayed out only if the value was between 15 and 21.

Weighting each possible total of dice 2 and 3 by these likelihoods puts most of the probability on totals of 10 or 11 (value 20 or 21). This raises the expected total to about 10.45, so fair value is about 20.4.

**Quote choice:**
- An ask just above 21 means an informed counterparty only buys from me if the value is 22 or more, which is unlikely.
- A bid just below 20 means an informed counterparty only sells to me if the value is 19 or less, which is also unlikely.
- Noise traders, with valuations around 20.4 plus or minus 5.8, still trade often at these prices, so I earn the spread from them.
- My short position of -1 is comfortable either way.

{"bid": 19.8, "ask": 21.1}

Fair value now is about 20.9. I'm quoting 19.8 / 22.3, roughly symmetric around it, since being short 2 doesn't call for much skew.

**Starting point.** Die 1 is 10. The expected value of die 2 is 2.5 and of die 3 is 6.25, so before using the trades the fair value is 18.75.

**Updating on the four quotes.** Let S be the sum of dice 2 and 3. For each quote, an informed trader acts deterministically on S, and a noise trader acts with a probability based on the fair value at that time. Each quote's likelihood is 0.5 for the informed case plus 0.5 times the noise probability:

| Quote | What happened | Informed would do this when | Likelihood |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (19.5 ask) | They bought | S ≥ 10 | 0.63 if S ≥ 10, else 0.13 |
| 2 (14 / 21) | No trade | 4 ≤ S ≤ 11 | 0.73 inside, 0.23 outside |
| 3 (15 / 22) | No trade | 5 ≤ S ≤ 12 | 0.72 inside, 0.22 outside |
| 4 (21.1 ask) | They bought | S ≥ 12 | 0.68 if S ≥ 12, else 0.18 |

I multiplied these likelihoods across all 64 equally likely (die 2, die 3) combinations. The posterior expected S is about 10.9, mostly concentrated on S = 10 to 12. So fair value is about 20.9.

**Quote.** A bid of 19.8 only gets hit by an informed trader if S ≤ 9, which has about 23% posterior probability. An ask of 22.3 only gets lifted by an informed trader if S ≥ 13, about 14%. That leaves reasonable edge against noise traders on both sides.

{"bid": 19.8, "ask": 22.3}

Fair value is about 19.4. The value is 10 plus die 2 plus die 3. I weighted each possible die 2 + die 3 sum by its prior probability and by how likely the five past trades were under it.

- Before trading, the expected sum of the two hidden dice is 2.5 + 6.25 = 8.75, so fair value was 18.75.
- The trade history pulls this up a little:
  - Stage 1 buy at 19.5 (raises it).
  - No trades at 14/21 and 15/22.
  - Buy at 21.1, then sell at 19.8 (these two conflict).
- The posterior mean of die 2 + die 3 is about 9.45, giving a fair value of about 19.4.
- Most of the probability sits on values 17 to 23. There is a thin tail from die 2 = 9 that reaches 26 to 28.

I checked several prices on each side. For each, I compared what I expect to earn from noise traders with what I expect to lose to informed traders:

**Ask side**

| Ask | Net expected gain |
|---|---|
| 21.1 | about 0.04 |
| 22.1 | about 0.25 |
| 24 | about 0.39 |
| 25 | about 0.40 |

**Bid side**

| Bid | Net expected gain |
|---|---|
| 18.1 | about 0.01 |
| 16.9 | about 0.29 |
| 15 | about 0.43 |
| 14.5 | about 0.43 |

Quoting wide on both sides gives the best expected profit. I'm short 1, so selling more stays well within the position limit.

{"bid": 15.0, "ask": 24.5}

I'm quoting a wide market around a fair value of about 20.3, bid 16.0 and ask 25.5.

**Fair value.** Die 1 = 10 and die 3 = 8, so the contract settles at 18 + die 2. The possible settlements are:

| Settlement | 18 | 19 | 20 | 22 | 27 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Faces | 3/8 | 1/8 | 1/8 | 2/8 | 1/8 |

On faces alone the mean is 20.5. I then updated on the stage‑2 trades, treating each counterparty as 50/50 informed or noise:
- **Quote 4:** someone bought at 21.1. That points to 22 or 27.
- **Quote 5:** someone sold at 19.8. That points to 18 or 19.
- **Quote 6:** nobody traded at 15/24.5. That argues against 27, because an informed trader would have bought.

These two trades can't both be informed. After the update the weights are about:

| Settlement | 18 | 19 | 20 | 22 | 27 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Weight | 0.40 | 0.13 | 0.05 | 0.36 | 0.07 |

That gives a public fair value of about 20.3.

**Ask.** Any ask between 22 and 27 only loses to an informed buyer if the value is 27, which has about 7% weight. Asks around 25–26 give the best balance between that loss and the edge from noise buyers, at about +0.43 expected.

**Bid.** Any bid at 18 or below never loses to an informed seller. Bids around 16–17 give the best edge from noise sellers, at about +0.49 expected.

Being short 1 makes little difference with this few quotes left.

{"bid": 16.0, "ask": 25.5}

Fair value is about 20.0.

**Settlement.** Settlement is 18 plus die 2. Die 1 = 10 and die 3 = 8 are known. Die 2 is one of 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 4, 4, 9, so settlement is 18, 18, 18, 19, 20, 22, 22 or 27.

**What quote 7 tells us.** I quoted 16 / 25.5 and nobody traded.
- An informed trader would have bought at 25.5 if the value were 27. So the no-trade lowers the chance of 27.
- A noise trader centred near 20.5 would have traded only about 23% of the time, so the no-trade carries some weight.
- Updated probabilities: 27 is about 6%, each of the other seven faces is about 13.5%.
- That gives a fair value of about 20.0.

**Choosing the ask.** Expected profit per quote is about 0.425 at an ask of 25 or 26. At 25 or above, the only informed trader who buys me out is the 27 case, which is about 6%. Noise buyers above the ask still pay a good margin.

**Choosing the bid.** Profit peaks at about 0.49 with a bid near 16. The lowest possible value is 18, so an informed trader will never sell to me below 18. Every fill at that bid comes from a noise trader.

The ±4 position limit is not a constraint at my current position of -1.

{"bid": 16, "ask": 25}

Only die 2 is still unknown, so settlement is 18 + die 2. That gives possible values of 18, 18, 18, 19, 20, 22, 22 or 27, each with prior probability 1/8.

**Updating on the trade history.** Informed traders make up half of all counterparties.
- **Stage 2 (die 3 not yet revealed):** someone bought at 21.1, which favours values above 21.1. Someone then sold at 19.8, which favours values below 19.8. The two roughly offset.
- **Stage 3 (quotes 7 and 8 at 16 / 25 and 25.5):** no trades. An informed trader holding 27 would have bought. Two misses therefore cut the weight on 27 sharply.

**Approximate posterior:**

| Value | 18 | 19 | 20 | 22 | 27 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 0.43 | 0.14 | 0.05 | 0.36 | 0.02 |

This gives a fair value of about 19.9.

**Choosing the quotes.** For each side I traded off what informed traders would take from me against what I earn from noise traders, whose valuations are about 19.9 ± 5.8.
- **Ask:** around 24.5 is best. Only the small chance of 27 exposes me there, and noise buyers still pay a wide margin.
- **Bid:** around 15.8 is best. It sits below every possible value, so informed sellers never hit it, and the noise margin is maximised there.

Being short 1 makes buying welcome, and the position limits allow either trade.

{"bid": 15.8, "ask": 24.5}

game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Three dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (8 faces, each equally likely): 0, 1, 3, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12.
- Die 2 (8 faces, loaded): 1 (prob 1/10), 1 (prob 1/10), 1 (prob 1/10), 7 (prob 1/10), 9 (prob 1/5), 9 (prob 1/5), 11 (prob 1/10), 11 (prob 1/10).
- Die 3 (8 faces, each equally likely): 1, 3, 3, 3, 5, 6, 9, 9.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
Fair value is the sum of the three expected die values:
- Die 1: 54/8 = 6.75
- Die 2: 0.3·1 + 0.1·7 + 0.4·9 + 0.2·11 = 6.8
- Die 3: 39/8 = 4.875

That gives a fair value of about 18.43. The settlement standard deviation is about 6.5, and half the counterparties know the outcome exactly. So I set a fairly wide spread, about ±4 around fair value. That keeps losses to informed traders small while still trading with noise traders.

{"bid": 14.4, "ask": 22.4}

The prior fair value is the sum of the three dice expectations:
- Die 1: 54/8 = 6.75
- Die 2: 0.3×1 + 0.1×7 + 0.4×9 + 0.2×11 = 6.8
- Die 3: 39/8 = 4.875

That gives a prior sum of about 18.4. The standard deviation is about 6.5, from variances of roughly 19.4 + 15.6 + 7.6.

**Updating on the sell at 14.4:**
- An informed trader sells only if the value is below 14.4. That happens with probability about 0.27, and the expected value in that case is about 10.5.
- A noise trader sells with about the same probability, 0.27, and tells us nothing about the value, so the expected value stays at 18.4.
- So a seller is equally likely to be either type. The posterior fair value is about 0.5×10.5 + 0.5×18.4 ≈ 14.5.

I'm long 1, so I'll centre slightly below 14.5. I'll keep a wide spread because the remaining uncertainty and adverse selection are still large.

{"bid": 10.8, "ask": 17.8}

Fair value is now about 10.8, and I'm skewing my quotes to reduce my long position of +2.

1. **Prior expected sum.** Die 1 averages 6.75, die 2 averages 6.8 and die 3 averages 4.875. That gives an expected sum of about 18.4.

2. **After quote 1 (sold at 14.4).**
   - If the seller was informed, the sum is at most 14 (probability about 0.29 under the prior).
   - A noise trader would sell there with probability about 0.27.
   - Updating on this trade moves fair value to about 14.3.

3. **After quote 2 (sold at 10.8).**
   - If the seller was informed, the sum is at most 10 (probability about 0.11 under the prior, with an average of about 6.8 in that case).
   - A noise trader would sell there with probability about 0.30.
   - Updating on this trade moves fair value to about **10.8**.

4. **Uncertainty.** The posterior is wide:
   - about 60% weight on a low sum, averaging about 6.8;
   - about 21% on a sum between 11 and 14;
   - about 18% on a sum above 14.

5. **Quote choice.** I'm long 2 and the evidence points to a low value, so I want to sell rather than buy.
   - Ask at 12.5, about 1.7 above fair value, to try to offload inventory.
   - Bid at 6.5, set low to avoid adding to the long against informed sellers when the sum is very low.

{"bid": 6.5, "ask": 12.5}

I'm long 3 units, so only an ask is allowed. The best ask by my estimate is about 12.5.

**Prior value of the remaining dice (die 3 = 3 is known):**
- Die 1 averages 6.75.
- Die 2 averages 6.8.
- So before using the trades, the contract is worth about 3 + 6.75 + 6.8 = 16.55.

**What the trades tell me:** Counterparties sold to me three times in a row, at 14.4, 10.8 and 6.5. An informed seller at 6.5 means the true value is below 6.5. That requires die 1 + die 2 to be 3 or less, meaning die 1 is 0 or 1 and die 2 is 1.
- I updated on these trades using rough estimates of the public fair value at each earlier quote.
- The updated value is about 5.9.
- About 82% of the probability is on a final value of 4 or 5.
- There is a thin upper tail of roughly 13%, mostly values of 10 or more.

**Choosing the ask:** For each candidate ask I added the expected gain from noise buyers and subtracted the expected loss from informed buyers.

| Ask | Net expected value of the sale |
|---|---|
| 7 | about −0.26 |
| 9 | about +0.13 |
| 11 | about +0.31 |
| 13 | about +0.35 |

The curve is flat between 12 and 13. A wide ask still sells to noise buyers fairly often, and it costs little when an informed trader buys because the value is high. I'll also have more chances to sell after die 2 is revealed.

{"bid": null, "ask": 12.5}

Fair value now looks like roughly 5.3, well below where I am long, so I'll keep only an ask and set it at 11.0.

**Fair value.** Die 3 is revealed as 3. Before any trading, die 1 averages 6.75 and die 2 averages 6.8. That gives a starting fair value of 16.55.

The trading history pulls that down sharply. I updated on the history using the 50/50 informed/noise mix in the rules, and my rough estimates of the public fair value at each earlier quote:
- Counterparties sold to me at bids of 14.4, then 10.8, then 6.5. The 6.5 sale points hard to an informed seller with a value below 6.5.
- No one bought at my 12.5 ask on quote 4.

After that update, about 86% of the probability sits on a settlement of 4 or 5 (die 1 = 0 or 1 with die 2 = 1). The posterior expected value is about **5.3**.

**Choosing the ask.** I am long 3, so only the ask matters. A high ask is mostly taken by noise traders, whose valuations centre near 5.3 with standard deviation 6.5, and I sell to them well above fair. It is rarely taken by informed traders, because the chance the value is that high is small.

Expected gain per quote at different asks:

| Ask | Expected gain |
|---|---|
| 6 | negative |
| 8 | about +0.25 |
| 10 | about +0.42 |
| 11 | about +0.44 |
| 12 | about +0.44 |

The curve is flat between 11 and 12. I'll quote just below the 12.5 that got no trade, at 11.0.

{"bid": null, "ask": 11.0}

Quoting ask only at 11.0, because that maximises my expected profit on this quote.

**Fair value**
- Die 3 is revealed as 3, so the settlement value is V = die 1 + die 2 + 3.
- With no trading history, the expected value would be 6.75 (die 1) + 6.8 (die 2) + 3 = 16.55.
- In stage 1, counterparties sold to me at all three of my falling bids (14.4, 10.8, 6.5). That pattern strongly suggests a low settlement value.
- In stage 2, nobody bought at my asks of 12.5 and 11. That also points to a low value.
- Updating on both, I estimate the public fair value at about 5.2. Most of the probability (around 87%) sits on V = 4 or 5. The rest is a small chance of a high outcome.

**Choosing the ask**
- If a noise trader buys from me, I gain the ask minus the value. If an informed trader buys, the true value is above my ask, so I lose.
- Expected profit from this quote at different asks:

| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 8 | about 0.29 |
| 10 | about 0.45 |
| 11 | about 0.46 |
| 12 | about 0.44 |

- The maximum is near 11. I'm already long 3, but my position limit doesn't change which ask is best here.

{"bid": null, "ask": 11.0}

Die 2 = 1 and die 3 = 3 are now known, so the settlement value is die 1 + 4.

**Estimating die 1.** On its own, die 1 averages 6.75. The stage-2 history changes that a lot.
- I asked 12.5, then 11, then 11, and nobody bought.
- If die 1 were 8 or more, an informed trader would have bought at 11 (value 12 or more is above 11). That happens half the time on each quote.
- Three no-trades in a row are therefore much more likely if die 1 is 0, 1 or 3.
- Assuming a noise trader stays out about 35% of the time, the posterior puts roughly 96% on die 1 being 0, 1 or 3.
- That gives an expected die 1 of about 1.6, so a fair value of about 5.6.

**Choosing the ask.** I am at the +3 limit, so I can only sell. I compared asks by the expected profit of one sale at that price:
- An ask of 7 or below sells to informed traders when the value is 7. That loses money.
- Asks between 9 and 12 mostly sell to noise traders well above fair value. The expected gain is about 0.4 to 0.5 per quote.
- The best range is about 10 to 12, where the expected gain is close to 0.5.

I'll ask 10.8.

{"bid": null, "ask": 10.8}

Die 2 = 1 and die 3 = 3 are now known, so the settlement value is 4 + die 1. That makes the possible values 4, 5, 7, 12, 13, 14, 15 or 16.

**Estimating the value from the trade history**
- In stage 1, counterparties sold to me three times, at bids of 14.4, 10.8 and 6.5. The sale at 6.5 points strongly to a value of 4 or 5, since an informed seller would only sell there if the value was below 6.5.
- In stages 2 and 3, no one bought at asks of 12.5, 11, 11 or 10.8. An informed buyer would have bought at those asks if the value were 12 or more, so high values are very unlikely.
- Putting both together, I estimate roughly 95% probability that the value is 4 or 5 and about 5% that it is 7. That gives a fair value of about 4.6.

**Choosing the ask**
I am long 3, and those units are already bought, so they don't affect this choice. What matters is the gain from selling one more unit: the ask minus the value.
- With the ask at 7 or above, an informed trader almost never buys, because the value is very unlikely to exceed it. Nearly all my fills come from noise traders.
- Noise traders value the contract at about 4.6 plus Normal noise with standard deviation 6.5. The expected gain is 0.5 × P(noise valuation > ask) × (ask − 4.6).
- That gain is about 0.42 at an ask of 7, 0.51 at 8, 0.548 at 9, 0.552 at 9.5 and 0.549 at 10. It is highest around 9.5.

{"bid": null, "ask": 9.5}

Settlement is 4 + die 1, since die 3 = 3 and die 2 = 1. Before trading, the possible values were 4, 5, 7, 12, 13, 14, 15 or 16, each equally likely.

**What the history says about die 1:**
- In stage 1, counterparties sold to me at 14.4, 10.8 and 6.5. The sale at 6.5 matters most: an informed trader sells there only if the value is below 6.5.
- In stages 2 and 3, nobody bought from me at asks of 12.5, 11, 11, 10.8 or 9.5.
- Both patterns point strongly to a low die 1.

**Posterior estimate (stage 1 and stage 3 trades only, stage 2 left out):**
- Value 4 or 5 (die 1 = 0 or 1): about 92%.
- Value 7 (die 1 = 3): about 8%.
- Value 12 or more: under 1%.
- That makes the public fair value about 4.8.

**Choosing the ask:** I am long 3 and can only sell. An informed trader buys only when the value is above my ask, which is very unlikely at any ask above 7. A noise trader buys when fair value plus N(0, 6.5) exceeds my ask, and each sale earns roughly the ask minus 4.8.

Expected profit from this quote at different asks:

| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 7 | about 0.38 |
| 8 | about 0.48 |
| 10 | about 0.54 |
| 11 | about 0.53 |

The best ask is around 10.

{"bid": null, "ask": 10.0}

game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Three dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (8 faces, each equally likely): 0, 1, 3, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12.
- Die 2 (8 faces, loaded): 1 (prob 1/10), 1 (prob 1/10), 1 (prob 1/10), 7 (prob 1/10), 9 (prob 1/5), 9 (prob 1/5), 11 (prob 1/10), 11 (prob 1/10).
- Die 3 (8 faces, each equally likely): 1, 3, 3, 3, 5, 6, 9, 9.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
I priced the contract by its expected sum and set the half-spread to maximise expected profit against the mix of informed and noise traders.

**Fair value**
- Die 1: (0+1+3+8+9+10+11+12)/8 = 6.75
- Die 2: 0.3·1 + 0.1·7 + 0.4·9 + 0.2·11 = 6.8
- Die 3: 39/8 = 4.875
- Fair value is 6.75 + 6.8 + 4.875 = **18.425**.

**Uncertainty**
- Variances are about 19.44 (die 1), 15.56 (die 2) and 7.61 (die 3).
- The total variance is about 42.6, so the standard deviation is about 6.5.
- That is the same size as the noise traders' spread (6.5).

**Spread choice**
I treated the settlement value as roughly Normal around fair value with standard deviation 6.5. For a half-spread h, write z = h/6.5. Expected profit per side is then about 0.5·6.5·(2z·Q(z) − φ(z)):
- Q(z) is the probability that a standard Normal exceeds z, and φ(z) is the standard Normal density at z.
- The 2z·Q(z) term is the gain from noise traders; the φ(z) term is the loss to informed traders.
- This peaks near z ≈ 1.2, so h ≈ 7.8.

My quote is 18.425 − 7.8 ≈ 10.6 on the bid and 18.425 + 7.8 ≈ 26.2 on the ask.

{"bid": 10.6, "ask": 26.2}

Fair value is about 18.4, and I'll quote roughly 7.2 either side of it: bid 11.2, ask 25.6.

**Fair value**
- Die 1 averages 54/8 = 6.75.
- Die 2 averages 0.3·1 + 0.1·7 + 0.4·9 + 0.2·11 = 6.8.
- Die 3 averages 39/8 = 4.875.
- The sum averages about 18.4, with variance 19.4 + 15.6 + 7.6 ≈ 42.6, so the standard deviation is about 6.5.

**Spread**
- The settlement value and noise-trader valuations both have a spread of about 6.5 around 18.4.
- Treating both as normal, the expected profit per quote at k standard deviations from fair is about σ(2kΦ̄(k) − φ(k)), where Φ̄(k) is the chance of being above k and φ is the normal density.
- That is positive and fairly flat between k ≈ 1.0 and 1.4. It peaks around k ≈ 1.2–1.25, which is about 8 points either side of fair.
- The real dice outcomes are lumpy rather than normal, so the formula is only a guide.
- The two earlier quotes, about 7.4–7.8 from fair, did not trade, which tells us little.
- I'll stay in that range, about 7.2 either side, slightly tighter than before.

{"bid": 11.2, "ask": 25.6}

Bid 6.0 and ask 19.6. The posterior mean is about 12.6, and the asymmetric quotes reflect that the distribution is lumpy, with heavy mass at 11 and a long upper tail.

**Prior given die 3 = 1.** Die 1 has mean 6.75 and die 2 has mean 6.8, so the settlement S = D1 + D2 + 1 has a prior mean of 14.55. Split by region:
- P(S ≤ 10) = 0.225
- P(S = 11) = 0.10
- P(S ≥ 12) = 0.675

**Updating on the trading history.** For each quote, the chance of what happened is 0.5 × (whether an informed trader would act that way) + 0.5 × (the noise trader's probability, around a public value of about 18.4).
- Quotes 1 and 2 had no trade. An informed trader would not trade there only if S ≥ 11.
- At quote 3 the counterparty sold at 11.2. An informed trader would do that only if S < 11.2.
- Combining these, the likelihoods are about 0.081 for S ≤ 10, 0.438 for S = 11 and 0.052 for S ≥ 12.

**Posterior.** The weights become roughly 19% for S ≤ 10, 45% for S = 11 and 36% for S ≥ 12. The mean is about 12.6.

**Choosing the ask.** I compared, for each ask level, the expected loss to informed buyers against the expected gain from noise buyers. The net gain is about +0.26 at 18, +0.37 at 20 and +0.36 at 21, so roughly 20 is best.

**Choosing the bid.** The same comparison on the buy side gives about +0.33 at 8, +0.39 at 6 and +0.38 at 5, so roughly 6 is best.

**Position adjustment.** I'm already long one unit, so I shade the ask down slightly to make a sale a bit more likely.

{"bid": 6.0, "ask": 19.6}

Using die 3 = 1 and the trades so far, I estimate fair value at about **10.5**. My bid and ask are set by weighing expected gains from noise traders against expected losses to informed traders.

**Prior for die 1 + die 2.** Die 1 averages 6.75 and die 2 averages 6.8. Their sum is spread from 1 to 23, with most weight between 9 and 12 and a second cluster between 17 and 21.

**What the history tells us**
- **Quote 3:** a counterparty sold at 11.2. That is much more likely if the total was below 11.2, which means die 1 + die 2 ≤ 10.
- **Quote 4:** there was no trade at 6 / 19.6. That points towards a total between 6 and 19.6, which means die 1 + die 2 between 5 and 18.
- **Posterior:** die 1 + die 2 averages about 9.45, so the settlement value averages about 10.45.
  - Most of the weight is on a total of 10 or 11, roughly 59% combined.
  - Low totals of 2–5 carry about 15%.
  - Totals of 12 or more carry about 19%.

**Ask.** The risk on this side is the upper tail, where an informed buyer would pay us about 16 or more on average.
- At 11.5 the expected loss to informed buyers outweighs the gain from noise traders.
- Between about 13 and 14 the expected result is positive, roughly +0.25 to +0.4.
- I quote 13.5.

**Bid.** The risk here is the low tail of 2–5.
- At 9.5 the expected result is negative.
- Between about 4 and 5 it is around +0.4 to +0.45.
- I am already long one unit, so I lean towards the lower end and bid 4.5.

{"bid": 4.5, "ask": 13.5}

Fair value is about 10.7. I'm quoting a wide spread, slightly skewed to sell because I'm long, at bid 5.5 and ask 15.5.

**Fair value**
- With die 3 = 1, the value is 1 + die 1 + die 2. Die 1 averages 6.75 and die 2 averages 6.8, so the prior expected value is 14.55.
- I treated each past quote as evidence: an informed trader sells below my bid, buys above my ask, and holds when the value is between them.
  - Quote 3: someone sold to me at 11.2.
  - Quote 4: no trade at 6 / 19.6.
  - Quote 5: no trade at 4.5 / 13.5.
- Updating on these three quotes moves the expected value down to about **10.7**. About 62% of the weight sits on values 10 and 11.

**Bid**
- An informed seller only hurts me when the value is below about 8, which has roughly 8% probability.
- Noise sellers below about 6 are profitable for me.
- The expected edge peaks at a bid of about 5–6, at roughly +0.5 per quote.

**Ask**
- The posterior has a fat right tail: values of 18 to 24 are possible when die 2 is 9 or 11.
- Asks of about 15–16 give the best expected edge, at roughly +0.4 per quote.
- I'm long 1, so I lean the ask slightly lower to make a sale more likely.

{"bid": 5.5, "ask": 15.5}

With dice 2 and 3 both revealed as 1, the settlement is 2 + die 1. Die 1 is uniform over {0, 1, 3, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12}, so the settlement can be 2, 3, 5, 10, 11, 12, 13 or 14.

**Updating on the earlier sale.** At quote 3 someone sold to me at 11.2.
- An informed seller would have done that only if the total was below 11.2, which means die 1 is 9 or lower.
- A noise trader would have sold only about 11% of the time, given the fair value then of about 19.1.
- Updating on this makes the low outcomes (2, 3, 5, 10, 11) much more likely than the high ones (12, 13, 14).
- The posterior fair value is about 6.6.

**Bid.** The outcomes split into a low cluster (2, 3, 5) and a high cluster (10 and up), so a bid near 7 does well.
- Informed traders sell to me only when the value is 2, 3 or 5, all well below 7, so I profit from them.
- Noise traders are centred near the fair value, so my loss to them is small.
- The expected edge is about +0.9 per quote, close to the best bid I found.

**Ask.** An ask near 12 is the best choice.
- Informed traders buy only when the value is 12 or more, and those outcomes are now unlikely.
- Noise trades at 12 earn about 5.4 each, roughly 20% of the time.
- The expected edge is about +0.5.

Position limits are not binding, since I am at +1 and can go to +3.

{"bid": 7.0, "ask": 12.0}

The settlement is now 2 + die 1, so it can only be 2, 3, 5, 10, 11, 12, 13 or 14.

**Estimating die 1 from the history**
- **Stage 1:** Quotes 1–2 had no trade at bids of 10.6 and 11, so an informed trader is unlikely to have held a sum of 10 or less. Quote 3 sold at 11.2, which favours a sum of 11 or less. Together these point mostly to die 1 = 9.
- **Stage 2:** Three quotes in a row had no trade. That makes die 1 = 0, 1 or 3 unlikely and makes 12 less likely.
- **Stage 3:** The buy at 12 shifts weight toward die 1 = 11 or 12, because an informed buyer there means a sum of 13 or 14.

**Posterior for the settlement**
- 11: about 55%
- 13: about 21%
- 10: about 10%
- 12: about 6%
- 14: about 5.5%
- 5 or below: about 2%

That gives an expected settlement (public fair value) of about **11.4**.

**Choosing the quote**
Each side earns from noise traders and loses to informed traders.
- **Ask:** Any ask below 14 gets hit by informed buyers. Expected profit rises to about 0.55 for asks between 16 and 17.
- **Bid:** Any bid above 5 risks the small mass at low sums. Expected profit is flat at about 0.52–0.53 for bids between 6 and 7.

I'll quote a bid of 6.5 and an ask of 16.4.

{"bid": 6.5, "ask": 16.4}

With die 2 and die 3 both showing 1, the known part of the sum is 2. Settlement is therefore 2 + die 1, so it is one of {2, 3, 5, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14}, each with prior probability 1/8.

**Updating on stage-3 trades**
- **Quote 7 (someone bought at 12):** This is about 4× more likely if the value is 13 or 14. In that case the likelihood is about 0.654, against about 0.154 for the other values.
- **Quote 8 (no trade at 6.5 / 16.4):** This makes the low values {2, 3, 5} less likely, because an informed trader would have sold there. The likelihood is about 0.776 for values 10–14 and about 0.276 for {2, 3, 5}.
- **Posterior:**

| Value | Probability (each) |
|---|---|
| 2, 3, 5 | ≈ 0.028 |
| 10, 11, 12 | ≈ 0.080 |
| 13, 14 | ≈ 0.338 |

The public fair value (expected settlement) is about 12.04.

**Choosing the quote**
- **Ask:** An ask above 14 can never be hit by an informed trader. Profit from noise traders peaks at an ask of about 17, worth about +0.55 expected.
- **Bid:** Expected profit is flat at about +0.42 for bids between 5.1 and 6. A bid of 6 gives about +0.42.

{"bid": 6, "ask": 17}

game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Three dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (6 faces, each equally likely): 5, 5, 6, 7, 8, 11.
- Die 2 (4 faces, loaded): 2 (prob 2/5), 2 (prob 1/10), 6 (prob 1/5), 8 (prob 3/10).
- Die 3 (4 faces, each equally likely): 7, 7, 8, 10.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
Expected settlement value is 7 + 4.6 + 8 = **19.6**, with a standard deviation of about 3.6.

**Die expectations**
- Die 1: (5+5+6+7+8+11)/6 = 7, variance about 4.33.
- Die 2: 2·0.5 + 6·0.2 + 8·0.3 = 4.6, variance about 7.24.
- Die 3: (7+7+8+10)/4 = 8, variance 1.5.
- Total variance is about 13.07.

**Choosing the half-spread**
Noise traders' valuations spread around the fair value with standard deviation 3.6. Informed traders know the true value, which is spread around the fair value with roughly the same width. For each half-spread I weighed the expected profit from noise trades against the expected loss to informed traders:

| Half-spread | Expected profit per side |
|---|---|
| 2 | ~0.15 |
| 3 | ~0.25 |
| 3.5 | ~0.27 |
| 4 | ~0.26 |

A half-spread of about 3.5 gives the highest expected profit. I am quoting 3.5 either side of 19.6.

{"bid": 16.1, "ask": 23.1}

The public fair value is 19.6, the sum of the three dice means:

- **Die 1:** (5+5+6+7+8+11)/6 = 7
- **Die 2:** 2·0.5 + 6·0.2 + 8·0.3 = 4.6
- **Die 3:** (7+7+8+10)/4 = 8

The settlement standard deviation is about 3.6 (variance 4.33 + 7.24 + 1.5 ≈ 13.1).

**Choosing the spread.** I compared, for each half-spread, the profit from noise traders against the expected loss to informed traders (35% of arrivals). This uses a normal approximation, since the real distribution is discrete.

- Net edge per quote side peaks at a half-spread of about 3.5 (≈ +0.27).
- A half-spread of 3.0 or 4.0 is slightly worse (≈ +0.25 to +0.26).

**Reading the history.** The no-trade at 16.1 / 23.1 was roughly symmetric around 19.6, so it tells me little. I'll keep the quote centred near 19.6 with a half-spread of about 3.4.

{"bid": 16.2, "ask": 23.0}

Expected sum = 7 (die 1) + 4.6 (die 2) + 8 (die 3) = **19.6**, with a standard deviation of about 3.6. Two quotes with no trade tell us almost nothing, so the public fair value stays near 19.6.

**Spread choice.** Both counterparty types have about the same spread around fair value: noise traders by construction, and informed traders because the settlement value's standard deviation is also about 3.6.

- With half-spread h and z = h/3.6, expected profit per side is proportional to z·Q(z) − 0.35·φ(z). Here Q(z) is the probability a standard normal exceeds z, and φ(z) is the standard normal density.
- This is maximised where Q(z) = 0.65·z·φ(z), which is at z ≈ 1.
- So the best half-spread is about 3.6.

This calculation treats the settlement value as normal, though the dice give a discrete, skewed distribution, so it is approximate.

I'll keep the quote centred on 19.6 with that half-spread.

{"bid": 16.1, "ask": 23.1}

Die 1 = 8 is revealed, so the settlement value is 8 + die 2 + die 3.
- Die 2 averages 2(0.5) + 6(0.2) + 8(0.3) = 4.6.
- Die 3 averages 8.
- So the public fair value is about 20.6.
- The possible settlement values are 17, 18, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24 and 26.
- The chances of those values are 0.25, 0.125, 0.125, 0.1, 0.05, 0.15, 0.125 and 0.075.
