**Ask:** I compared expected profit per quote for several ask levels. Noise buyers are profitable, while informed buyers lose me money when the value is above my ask.
- An ask of 23 gives about +0.27.
- An ask of 24 gives about +0.33. Here informed buyers only cost me when the value is 26.
- An ask of 24.5 gives about +0.31.
- I'll quote 24.

**Bid:** The lowest possible value is 17. A bid of 17.0 is only hit by informed sellers if their value is strictly below 17, which can't happen. Noise sellers then give an expected profit of about +0.37. Bidding higher than 17 lets informed sellers hit me whenever the value is 17, which reduces the expected profit.

{"bid": 17.0, "ask": 24.0}

Die 1 is revealed as 8, so the settlement value is 8 + die 2 + die 3.

**Fair value**
- Die 2 has an expected value of 0.5·2 + 0.2·6 + 0.3·8 = 4.6.
- Die 3 has an expected value of 8.
- So the public fair value is 8 + 4.6 + 8 = **20.6**.

The possible settlement values and their probabilities are:

| Value | 17 | 18 | 20 | 21 | 22 | 23 | 24 | 26 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | .25 | .125 | .125 | .10 | .05 | .15 | .125 | .075 |

**Ask**
For each ask, I added the expected profit from noise traders who buy above it. I then subtracted the expected loss to informed traders whose value is above the ask.

| Ask | Net expected profit |
|---|---|
| 23 | ≈ 0.27 |
| 23.5 | ≈ 0.31 |
| 24 | ≈ 0.33 |
| 24.5 | ≈ 0.31 |

The best ask is 24.

**Bid**
- At a bid of 17, informed traders never sell. Their lowest possible value is 17, and they only sell if their value is strictly below the bid.
- The noise-trader profit at 17 is about 0.37.
- A bid of 17.5 gives about 0.35, because it loses to informed traders holding a value of 17.
- A bid of 16.9 gives about 0.365.

The best bid is 17.

{"bid": 17, "ask": 24}

Die 1 is revealed as 8. The expected values of the other two dice are:
- Die 2: 2·0.5 + 6·0.2 + 8·0.3 = 4.6
- Die 3: 8

So the public fair value is 8 + 4.6 + 8 = 20.6.

**Possible settlement values:**
- 17 with probability 0.25
- 18 with probability 0.125
- 20 with probability 0.125
- 21 with probability 0.10
- 22 with probability 0.05
- 23 with probability 0.15
- 24 with probability 0.125
- 26 with probability 0.075

**Ask:** At 24.0, an informed trader buys only when the value is 26. That is an expected loss of about 0.05. Noise traders buy about 17% of the time, earning 3.4 each time, which is worth about 0.38. The net is roughly +0.33 per quote, which is close to the best of the asks I checked.

**Bid:** At 17.0, an informed trader never sells, because the lowest value is 17 and they sell only if their value is strictly below my bid. Noise traders sell about 16% of the time, earning 3.6 each time. That is worth about +0.37, again close to the best I checked.

{"bid": 17.0, "ask": 24.0}

Dice 1 and 2 are revealed, so their sum is 8 + 6 = 14. Die 3 shows 7, 7, 8 or 10 with equal chance. The settlement value is therefore 21 (probability 1/2), 22 (1/4) or 24 (1/4), and fair value is 22.

**Ask side.** An informed trader only buys when the value is above my ask. With an ask of 24 or higher, the informed trader never buys, so only noise traders (valuation 22 + N(0, 3.6)) reach it. Expected edge per quote on this side is 0.65 × P(noise valuation > a) × (a − 22):
- a = 24: about 0.376
- a = 25: about 0.394 (the best)
- a = 26: about 0.347

Asks between 22 and 24 do worse, because they also lose to informed buyers when the value is 24.

**Bid side.** An informed trader only sells when the value is below my bid. With a bid of 21 or lower, the informed trader never sells. The same calculation for noise sellers peaks at a bid of 19, with edge about 0.394.

Both sides are symmetric around 22, and my position is flat, so I quote 19 / 25.

{"bid": 19.0, "ask": 25.0}

Dice 1 and 2 are known (8 + 6 = 14), so settlement depends only on die 3. The possible values are 21 (probability 1/2), 22 (1/4) and 24 (1/4). The public fair value is 22. Earlier no-trades don't shift it, because both quotes were wide.

**Ask side:**
- An ask of 24.0 or higher never sells to an informed trader, since no settlement value is above 24.
- With noise standard deviation 3.6, expected profit per quote from noise buyers is 0.65 × P(valuation > ask) × (ask − 22).
- This is roughly flat between 24.5 and 25 and peaks near 24.8, at about +0.40 per quote.

**Bid side:**
- A bid at or below 21 never buys from an informed trader.
- A bid between 21 and 22 loses money, because informed traders sell whenever the value is 21.
- By symmetry with the ask, the noise-only profit peaks near 22 − 2.8 = 19.2, at about +0.40 per quote.

{"bid": 19.2, "ask": 24.8}

Dice 1 and 2 are already revealed at 8 and 6, so the sum is 14 plus die 3. Die 3 is 7, 7, 8 or 10 with equal chance. Settlement is therefore 21 (prob 1/2), 22 (prob 1/4) or 24 (prob 1/4), with a fair value of 22.

**Ask side.** An ask between 22 and 24 loses to an informed buyer whenever the value is 24. Above 24 informed traders never buy, so only noise traders trade there. Profit from noise traders, 0.65·x·P(N > x), peaks at about x = 2.7 above fair value, earning about 0.40 per quote. That gives an ask of about 24.7.

**Bid side.** A bid above 21 loses to an informed seller half the time, when the value is 21. Below 21 only noise traders sell. By the same calculation the best spread is about 2.7 below fair value, so a bid of about 19.3.

Since this is the last quote, there is no future quote to protect.

{"bid": 19.3, "ask": 24.7}

game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Three dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (6 faces, each equally likely): 5, 5, 6, 7, 8, 11.
- Die 2 (4 faces, loaded): 2 (prob 2/5), 2 (prob 1/10), 6 (prob 1/5), 8 (prob 3/10).
- Die 3 (4 faces, each equally likely): 7, 7, 8, 10.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
The fair value before any reveals is the sum of the three dice's expected values:

- **Die 1:** mean 7, variance 4.33
- **Die 2:** mean 0.5·2 + 0.2·6 + 0.3·8 = 4.6, variance 7.24
- **Die 3:** mean 8, variance 1.5

The total fair value is **19.6**. The total variance is 13.07, so the standard deviation is about 3.6.

To pick the spread, I treat the settlement value as roughly normal with standard deviation 3.6, the same as the noise traders' spread. On each side I earn the half-spread from noise traders but lose to the 35% of informed traders whose value lies past my quote. Testing a few half-spreads, a half-spread near 3.6 (about one standard deviation) gives the highest expected profit per side. That puts the quotes at about 16.0 and 23.2.

{"bid": 16.0, "ask": 23.2}

The public fair value has moved up to about 21.5 after the buy at 23.2, so I'm centring my quotes there with a wide spread.

**Prior expected sum**
- Die 1: 42/6 = 7
- Die 2: 0.5·2 + 0.2·6 + 0.3·8 = 4.6
- Die 3: 32/4 = 8
- Total: **19.6**. The sum ranges from 14 to 29.

**Update from the buy at 23.2**
- Since all faces are whole numbers, a value above 23.2 means a sum of at least 24. P(S ≥ 24) ≈ 0.142, and E[S | S ≥ 24] ≈ 25.6.
- An informed trader buys only if the value is above 23.2. A noise trader buys with probability P(19.6 + N > 23.2) = P(Z > 1) ≈ 0.16.
- If S ≥ 24, the chance of this buy is 0.35 + 0.65·0.16 ≈ 0.45. If S ≤ 23, it is 0.65·0.16 ≈ 0.10.
- Weighting the high case (mean ≈ 25.6) against the low case (mean ≈ 18.6) gives a posterior mean of **≈ 21.5**.

**Quote**
- The value is still very uncertain, and the informed share is high (0.35), so the spread stays wide.
- I am short 1, so I tilt the quotes slightly upward.
- Bid 19.5 and ask 24.5 each sit about 3 below or above the new fair value. That still trades with roughly 20% of noise traders on each side.

{"bid": 19.5, "ask": 24.5}

Fair value is about 21.8, so I'll quote around it with a spread of about 3.4.

**Prior expectation**
- Die 1 averages 7.
- Die 2 averages 4.6 (2×0.5 + 6×0.2 + 8×0.3).
- Die 3 averages 8.
- The prior mean is 19.6, with a standard deviation of about 3.6.

**Quote 1: they bought at 23.2.**
- Before that trade, the value had only about an 18% chance of being above 23.2.
- A buy was much more likely if the value was high. Informed and noise traders together give a 0.45 chance of a buy when the value is above 23.2, versus 0.10 when it is below.
- That makes a high value and a low value roughly equally likely. The posterior mean moves up to about 22.2.

**Quote 2: no trade at 19.5 / 24.5.**
- No trade is about twice as likely when the value lies between 19.5 and 24.5 (likelihood about 0.68 versus 0.33).
- This shrinks the extreme outcomes. The fair value settles at about 21.8.

**Quote**
- I am short 1, which is fine, so I quote close to symmetric around 21.8.
- A spread of about 3.4 allows for adverse selection from informed traders.

{"bid": 20.2, "ask": 23.6}

Die 1 = 11 is revealed, so the settlement is 11 + Die 2 + Die 3.

**Fair value**
- Die 2 has mean 2(0.5) + 6(0.2) + 8(0.3) = 4.6.
- Die 3 has mean (7 + 7 + 8 + 10)/4 = 8.
- Expected settlement is 11 + 4.6 + 8 = 23.6.
- The stage-1 trades pointed both ways (a buy at 23.2, a sell at 20.2), so they add little information.

**Settlement distribution**

| Value | Probability |
|---|---|
| 20 | 0.25 |
| 21 | 0.125 |
| 23 | 0.125 |
| 24 | 0.10 |
| 25 | 0.05 |
| 26 | 0.15 |
| 27 | 0.125 |
| 29 | 0.075 |

**Choosing each side**
For each price I weighed noise-trader profit against expected losses to informed traders.

- **Ask:** a 26.9 ask loses to informed buyers only when the value is 27 or 29, costing about 0.06. Noise buyers earn about 0.39. That nets about +0.33 per quote, higher than 25.5, 26.5 or 27.5.
- **Bid:** a 20.0 bid is never hit by an informed seller, because the lowest possible value is 20 and a tie does not trade. Noise sellers earn about 0.37, which beats 20.5, 20.9 and 21.5.

{"bid": 20.0, "ask": 26.9}

With die 1 = 11 revealed, the settlement is 11 + die 2 + die 3, and its expected value is 23.6.

**Settlement distribution**
- Expected die 2 = 0.5·2 + 0.2·6 + 0.3·8 = 4.6.
- Expected die 3 = 8.
- Fair value = 11 + 4.6 + 8 = 23.6.

| Total | Probability |
|---|---|
| 20 | 0.25 |
| 21 | 0.125 |
| 23 | 0.125 |
| 24 | 0.10 |
| 25 | 0.05 |
| 26 | 0.15 |
| 27 | 0.125 |
| 29 | 0.075 |

The distribution has clusters at 20 and at 26 to 29. That makes quotes close to fair value expensive against informed traders.

**Choosing the quotes**

For each candidate quote I weighed the expected gain from noise traders against the expected loss to informed traders. Profit is measured against fair value 23.6.

| Ask | Net expected profit |
|---|---|
| 24.5 | negative |
| 25.5 | ≈ 0.19 |
| 26.5 | ≈ 0.31 |
| 27.0 | ≈ 0.33 (best) |

At 27.0 an informed trader whose value is exactly 27 does not trade, so I only lose to a value of 29.

| Bid | Net expected profit |
|---|---|
| 20.0 | ≈ 0.37 |
| 20.3 to 20.5 | ≈ 0.35 to 0.36 |
| 21.0 | ≈ 0.31 |

At 20.0 an informed trader whose value is 20 does not trade, so the informed loss is zero. A bid of 20.0 to 20.4 is roughly as good as anything else. I chose 20.4, which gives up very little and fills a bit more often.

{"bid": 20.4, "ask": 27.0}

Fair value is about 23.5, and I'm quoting bid 20.4 / ask 26.9.

**Fair value.** Die 1 is 11. The remaining sum (die 2 + die 3) has 8 possible totals: 9, 10, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16 and 18. That puts the settlement value in {20, 21, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 29}.
- In quote 4 (bid 20, ask 26.9) nobody bought. That makes 27 and 29 less likely, because an informed trader would have bought.
- In quote 5 (bid 20.4) nobody sold. That makes 20 less likely, because an informed trader would have sold.

After these updates the expected value is about **23.5**.

**Quote choice.** I compared expected profit for different prices, counting both informed and noise traders:
- **Ask ~26.9:** the informed trader buys only when the value is 29, which is unlikely. Noise traders buy about 17% of the time with roughly 3.4 of edge.
- **Bid ~20.4:** the informed trader sells only when the value is 20, a small loss of 0.4. Noise traders sell about 20% of the time with roughly 3.1 of edge.

{"bid": 20.4, "ask": 26.9}

Die 1 = 11 and die 2 = 8 are known, so 19 is locked in. Only die 3 is left: 7, 7, 8 or 10, each with probability 1/4.

**Settlement and fair value**
- The settlement value is 26 with probability 1/2, 27 with probability 1/4, and 29 with probability 1/4.
- Its expected value is 27, so the public fair value is 27.

**Choosing the quotes**
- An informed trader buys only if 29 is above my ask, and sells only if 26 is below my bid.
- Keeping the ask above 29 and the bid below 26 means informed traders never trade against me. Only noise traders, valued at 27 plus Normal noise with SD 3.6, will trade.
- Expected profit from the ask is 0.65 × P(noise > a − 27) × (a − 27). This is roughly flat between 29.5 and 29.8 at about 0.397, so I quote 29.7.
- The bid side mirrors this. Expected profit is about 0.398 at a bid of 24.3, so I quote 24.3.
- A bid between 26 and 27 does worse. For example, a bid of 26.5 makes about 0.145 from noise traders but loses about 0.0875 to informed sellers when the value is 26.

{"bid": 24.3, "ask": 29.7}

Dice 1 and 2 are known (11 + 8 = 19). Die 3 is 7, 7, 8 or 10 with equal chance. So the settlement is 26 (prob 1/2), 27 (1/4) or 29 (1/4), and the public fair value is 27.

- **Ask:** At 29 or above, an informed trader never buys from me, because the value is never strictly above my ask. Against noise traders, I compared expected profit at several prices from 29 up to 30. The best is about 27 + 2.7 = 29.7, giving about 0.40 expected profit.
- **Bid:** At 26 or below, an informed trader never sells to me. The same calculation for noise traders gives a best bid of 27 − 2.7 = 24.3, also about 0.40 expected profit.

{"bid": 24.3, "ask": 29.7}

This is the last quote, so I only need to price against the final settlement value.

**Settlement value.** Die 1 (11) and die 2 (8) are known, so the sum so far is 19. Die 3 (7, 7, 8, 10) leaves these outcomes:

| Settlement | Probability |
|---|---|
| 26 | 1/2 |
| 27 | 1/4 |
| 29 | 1/4 |

The expected settlement is 27.

**What the history tells me.** At quote 8 someone bought at 29.7. An informed trader would not do that, because the highest possible value is 29. So it must have been a noise trader, and the trade tells me nothing about die 3. The public fair value stays about 27.

**Ask side.** An ask of 29 or higher is never hit by an informed trader. Only noise traders buy, so the expected profit is about 0.65 × (a − 27) × P(noise valuation > a).
- At 29.7 this gives about 0.40.
- At 30.0 it gives about 0.39.

The peak is around 29.7 to 29.8. Lower asks, such as 28, attract informed buyers when the value is 29 and earn less.

**Bid side.** A bid of 26 or lower is never hit by an informed trader. By the same calculation for noise sellers, the best bid is around 24.2 to 24.3.

My position of −1 leaves room to trade on either side, so I quote both.

{"bid": 24.2, "ask": 29.8}

game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Three dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (8 faces, each equally likely): 3, 6, 7, 8, 8, 10, 11, 11.
- Die 2 (6 faces, each equally likely): 0, 2, 4, 8, 8, 10.
- Die 3 (8 faces, each equally likely): 0, 1, 6, 8, 8, 9, 10, 10.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
Fair value is about 19.8, with standard deviation about 5.7.

**Expected values of the dice**
- Die 1: 64/8 = 8
- Die 2: 32/6 ≈ 5.33
- Die 3: 52/8 = 6.5
- Expected sum ≈ 19.83

**Uncertainty**
- Variance of the sum ≈ 6.5 + 12.9 + 13.5 = 32.9.
- So the standard deviation is about 5.7, the same size as the noise traders' spread.

**Quote**
I quote a half-spread of about 3.5 around 19.8. This trades off the profit from noise traders against losses to informed traders. Those losses are large here because no information has been revealed yet.

{"bid": 16.3, "ask": 23.4}

Fair value is about 19.83, the sum of the three dice means (8 + 5.33 + 6.5). The standard deviation of the sum is about 5.7. The last quote, roughly ±3.5 around fair value, did not trade, which tells us little. I'll keep a similar spread, slightly tighter, to protect against informed traders while still giving noise traders a chance to trade.

{"bid": 16.5, "ask": 23.2}

Fair value is about 23.3, so I quote 20.6 / 26.2, skewed slightly upward because I'm short one unit.

**Prior expectation with die 3 revealed as 8:**
- Die 1 mean is 64/8 = 8.
- Die 2 mean is 32/6 ≈ 5.33.
- Prior fair value is 8 + 5.33 + 8 ≈ 21.33.

**Update for the buy at 23.2 in stage 1:**
- Stage-1 fair value was 8 + 5.33 + 6.5 ≈ 19.83.
- A noise trader buys at 23.2 if its valuation exceeds it, which happens with probability P(Z > 0.59) ≈ 0.28.
- So the chance of a buy was about 0.35 + 0.65 × 0.28 ≈ 0.53 if the value was above 23.2, and about 0.18 otherwise.
- With die 3 = 8, a value above 23.2 means die 1 + die 2 ≥ 16. That covers 17 of the 48 combinations, whose sums add to 307. The other 31 combinations add to 333.
- Weighting by those buy probabilities, E[die 1 + die 2] = (0.53 × 307 + 0.18 × 333) / (0.53 × 17 + 0.18 × 31) ≈ 15.26.
- Public fair value is therefore about 23.26.

**Quote:**
- I set the bid and ask roughly 2.7 to 2.9 away from fair value. That keeps the spread wide enough against informed traders and still catches noise traders, whose spread is 5.7.

{"bid": 20.6, "ask": 26.2}

The public fair value is about 23. I'm quoting roughly 2.2 below it and 2.6 above, leaning slightly up because I'm short one unit.

**Prior mean of the remaining dice**
- Die 1 has a mean of 8 and a variance of 6.5.
- Die 2 has a mean of about 5.33 and a variance of about 12.9.
- With die 3 revealed as 8, the prior mean of the sum is about 21.33. The standard deviation still to resolve is about 4.4.

**Effect of the stage-1 buy at my 23.2 ask**
- An informed trader buys at 23.2 if die 1 + die 2 > 15.2. The chance of that is 17/48, about 0.35.
- If it is above 15.2, die 1 + die 2 averages about 18.1. Otherwise it averages about 10.7.
- In stage 1 the public fair value was about 19.8. A noise trader would buy at 23.2 with probability about 0.27.
- Weighing informed and noise traders, the buy raises the chance of the high case to about 0.62. That puts the expected die 1 + die 2 near 15.3, so a sum of about 23.3.

**Effect of no trade at 20.6 / 26.2**
This trims the extremes on both sides a little. Fair value stays near 23.

**Quote**
- Bid 20.8, about 2.2 below fair.
- Ask 25.6, about 2.6 above fair.

The spread allows for the 35% chance that the counterparty is informed. I set the ask a little further out than the bid because I'm already short one unit.

{"bid": 20.8, "ask": 25.6}

Die 1 = 8 and die 3 = 8 give 16, so settlement is 16 + die 2, which is one of 16, 18, 20, 24, 24 or 26.

**Updating die 2 from the trading history**
- **Quote 2 (they bought at 23.2):** Public fair value then was 19.83. An informed buyer here means die 2 is 8 or 10. A noise trader buys about 28% of the time.
- **Quote 4 (they sold at 20.8):** Public fair value then was 21.33. An informed seller here means die 2 is 0, 2 or 4. A noise trader sells about 46% of the time.
- **Combined weights:** about 0.141 each for die 2 = 0, 2, 4 and 0.193 each for die 2 = 8, 8, 10.
- **Fair value:** expected die 2 is about 5.85, so fair value is about 21.85.

**Choosing the quotes**
- **Ask:** Expected profit rises toward an ask just above 26. At that level informed traders never buy (26 is the highest possible settlement). Noise traders still buy about 23% of the time, at about 4.25 above fair. Expected profit is about 0.63.
- **Bid:** Expected profit peaks around 16.4–16.5. Informed traders only sell when settlement is 16, a small loss. Noise traders sell about 17% of the time, at about 5.4 below fair. Expected profit is about 0.58.

{"bid": 16.4, "ask": 26.1}

With die 3 = 8 and die 1 = 8 revealed, the known part is 16. Only die 2 is still hidden, so settlement can only be 16, 18, 20, 24, 24 or 26.

**Updating on the last quote.** At quote 5 nobody traded against my 16.4 bid and 26.1 ask. If the settlement were 16, an informed trader would have sold to me at 16.4. So "no trade" makes 16 less likely and every other outcome slightly more likely.

- Before quote 5, the fair value was 21.33.
- At that value, a noise trader declines to trade with probability about 0.605.
- After the update, the probabilities are roughly: 16 at 9.6%, 18 at 18.1%, 20 at 18.1%, 24 at 36.2%, 26 at 18.1%.
- The new public fair value is about 21.8.

**Ask.** The highest possible settlement is 26, so an ask just above 26 loses nothing to informed traders.
- An ask of 26.1 earns about 0.63 from noise traders.
- An ask of 24.1 earns only about 0.40, because an informed buyer takes it when the value is 26.
- Asks above 26.1 earn slightly less, so 26.1 is the best choice.

**Bid.**
- A bid of 16.0 avoids informed sellers entirely and earns about 0.58.
- Raising the bid toward 17 brings in more noise trades. It only risks a small, low-probability loss if the value is 16.
- The best range is about 16.5–17, worth around 0.59. I'll bid 16.8.

{"bid": 16.8, "ask": 26.1}

game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Three dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (4 faces, each equally likely): 1, 5, 7, 10.
- Die 2 (6 faces, each equally likely): 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 12.
- Die 3 (8 faces, each equally likely): 0, 0, 1, 6, 6, 7, 11, 11.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
The fair value is the sum of the three dice's expected values, 16. I quote 10.5 / 21.5, which is 5.5 either side of fair value.

**Expected values**
- Die 1: (1+5+7+10)/4 = 5.75
- Die 2: (1+2+3+4+8+12)/6 = 5.00
- Die 3: (0+0+1+6+6+7+11+11)/8 = 5.25
- Sum: 16.0

**Spread**
- The standard deviation of the sum is about 6.6, close to the noise traders' spread of 6.6.
- Each side's expected profit is the gain from noise traders crossing the quote minus the loss to informed traders.

| Distance from 16 | Expected profit per side |
|---|---|
| 4 | about 0.65 |
| 5 | about 0.73 |
| 6 | about 0.74 |

The profit curve is flat between 5 and 6, so I use 5.5.

{"bid": 10.5, "ask": 21.5}

Fair value is about 16.0. The die means are 5.75, 5.0 and 5.25. Since no trade happened at the last quote, I have no new information to move it either way. The settlement standard deviation is about 6.6, close to the noise traders' 6.6. I approximated both as Normal. On that basis, the expected profit per side peaks at a half-spread of roughly 5.9. That trades off the 0.8 chance of a noise trader against the 0.2 chance of an informed one. I'm using a half-spread of 5.8 around 16.

{"bid": 10.2, "ask": 21.8}

Fair value is about **16.0**, and I'm quoting about 5.9 either side of it: bid 10.1, ask 21.9.

**Fair value.** Each die's expected value:
- Die 1: (1 + 5 + 7 + 10) / 4 = 5.75
- Die 2: (1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 8 + 12) / 6 = 5
- Die 3: 42 / 8 = 5.25

They add to 16.0. Nothing has traded yet, so there is no history to move it.

**Spread of the settlement value.** The variances of the three dice add to about 43.3. That gives a standard deviation of about 6.6, the same as the noise traders' spread.

**Choosing the half-spread h.** On each side I compare:
- what I earn from noise traders: 0.8 · h · Q(h/6.6), where Q is the chance a standard normal exceeds that value;
- what I lose to informed traders: 0.2 · 6.6 · (φ(x) − x·Q(x)), where x = h/6.6 and φ is the standard normal density.

The expected profit per side works out to 6.6 · [x·Q(x) − 0.2·φ(x)]. Checking a few values:
- x = 0.8 gives 0.1116
- x = 0.9 gives 0.1124
- x = 1.0 gives 0.110

The best is around x ≈ 0.9, so h is about 5.9.

{"bid": 10.1, "ask": 21.9}

Fair value given die 3 = 6 and the earlier buy at 21.9 is about 18.3:

- **Prior.** Die 1 averages 5.75, die 2 averages 5, and die 3 is 6, so the prior is 16.75.
- **The buy at 21.9 in stage 1.** It raises the chance of the high combinations where die 1 + die 2 ≥ 16. An informed trader would only buy there, and a noise trader buys about 15% of the time. Weighting by that pushes the estimate up to about 18.3.

I compared, for each price, what I gain from noise traders against what I lose to informed traders:

- **Ask:** the expected edge is largest around 24, at about +0.80 per quote.
- **Bid:** the expected edge is largest around 12 to 13, at about +0.79 per quote.

Being short 1 has little effect, so I quote close to those levels.

{"bid": 13.0, "ask": 24.0}

Fair value is about 16.5, so I'll quote 12.0 bid and 21.0 ask, about ±4.5 around it.

**Starting estimate.** Die 1 averages 5.75 and die 2 averages 5. With die 3 revealed as 6, the starting expected value is 16.75.

**Updating on the trading history.** I treated each past quote as evidence about the value of die 1 plus die 2, since die 3 is now known. Each counterparty is informed with probability 0.2 and a noise trader otherwise.
- **Quotes 1 and 2 (no trade):** An informed trader would not trade only if die 1 + die 2 was between 5 and 15. That made those middle sums more likely.
- **Quote 3 (they bought at 21.9):** An informed trader would buy only if die 1 + die 2 was 16 or more. That made the high sums (17, 18, 19, 22) more likely.
- **Quote 4 (they sold at 13):** An informed trader would sell only if die 1 + die 2 was 6 or less. That made the low sums (2 to 6) more likely.

Weighting all 24 combinations of die 1 and die 2 by these effects gives an expected die 1 + die 2 of about 10.5. Adding die 3 gives a fair value of about 16.5.

**Quote width.** Die 1 and die 2 are still unknown and the value spread is wide. Noise traders' valuations also scatter with a standard deviation of 6.6. So I keep about ±4.5 around fair value to protect against informed traders while still trading with noise traders.

{"bid": 12.0, "ask": 21.0}

Fair value is about 15.8, so I'm centring my quote there with a spread to cover the chance of facing an informed trader.

1. **Prior mean.** Die 3 is revealed as 6. Die 1 averages 5.75 and die 2 averages 5. That gives a public mean of 16.75 before using the trades.

2. **Possible settlement values.** The 24 equally likely (die 1, die 2) combinations give totals from 8 to 28.

3. **Quote 4: they sold to me at 13.**
   - If the true value is below 13, the chance of that sale is 0.2 (informed) + 0.8 × 0.285 (noise) ≈ 0.43.
   - If the true value is 13 or more, only a noise trader would sell, so the chance is 0.8 × 0.285 ≈ 0.23.
   - The noise figure is the chance a noise valuation falls below 13. That uses a public fair value of 16.75 and a standard deviation of 6.6.
   - So this trade makes values below 13 about 1.9 times as likely as before.

4. **Quote 5: no trade at 12 / 21.**
   - If the true value is between 12 and 21, the chance of no trade is about 0.2 + 0.8 × 0.50 ≈ 0.60.
   - Outside that range, an informed trader would have traded, so the chance is about 0.8 × 0.50 ≈ 0.40.
   - The 0.50 is the chance a noise trader would not trade at these prices, using a fair value of about 16.

5. **Posterior.** Weighting each of the 24 outcomes by these two likelihoods gives a fair value of about 15.8.

6. **Quote.** I'm at a flat position, so I set a symmetric spread around 15.8. It is slightly tighter than last quote's 12/21, which drew no trade.

{"bid": 12.6, "ask": 19.2}

Die 1 = 7 and die 3 = 6 are revealed, so the contract settles at 13 + die 2. Die 2 is one of {1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 12}, so settlement is one of {14, 15, 16, 17, 21, 25}. With no other information, die 2 averages 5, giving a fair value of 18.

**What the earlier trades tell us**
- Quote 6, a buy at 19.2: an informed trader would only buy if die 2 is 8 or 12. This raises the weight on high values.
- Quotes 1, 2 and 5 had no trade. An informed trader would have bought if die 2 were 12, so these lower the weight on 12.
- Quote 3, a buy at 21.9: an informed trader would only buy if die 2 is 12. This raises the weight on 12.
- Quote 4, a sell at 13: no informed trader would sell, because settlement is at least 14. So this trade carries no information.

**Estimated settlement after the history**
- 14 to 17: about 57% combined
- 21: about 24%
- 25: about 19%
- Fair value: about 18.6

**Choosing the quotes**
For each candidate price, I weighed profit from noise traders (valuations around 18.6, standard deviation 6.6) against losses to informed traders (probability 0.2).
- Ask: expected profit keeps rising up to about 23.5–24.5, where the only informed loss is the value-25 case. I chose 23.8.
- Bid: expected profit is highest at about 13.9–14. At a bid below 14, an informed trader never sells to me.

{"bid": 13.9, "ask": 23.8}

Dice 3 and 1 are revealed (6 + 7 = 13). Die 2 averages 5, so the possible settlements are 14, 15, 16, 17, 21 or 25, with a prior mean of 18.

**Update from quote 7 (13.9 / 23.8, no trade).**
- An informed trader with value 25 would have bought at 23.8.
- So "no trade" makes 25 less likely: about 0.12 weight against about 0.176 for each other outcome.
- The updated fair value is about **17.6**.

**Ask side.** With noise of standard deviation 6.6, I weighed the noise-trader edge against losses to informed buyers. Above 21, the only informed buyer is the one holding 25.
- At 22.5 the expected profit is about 0.84.
- At 23 it is also about 0.84.
- So the best ask is about 22.8.

**Bid side.** Keeping the bid below 14 avoids losing to informed sellers.
- At 13 the expected profit is about 0.89.
- At 12.5 it is about 0.90.
- So the best bid is about 12.8.

A position of -1 leaves plenty of room within the limits, so the quote stays roughly symmetric around fair.

{"bid": 12.8, "ask": 22.8}

This is the last quote and my position is flat, so I set each side to maximise its own expected profit.

**Fair value.** The revealed dice give 6 + 7 = 13, so settlement is 13 plus die 2. That makes the possible values 14, 15, 16, 17, 21 or 25. With equal weights the mean is 18.

**What the trading history implies.**
- Quote 7 (13.9 / 23.8), no trade: an informed trader would have bought if the value were 25, so no trade makes 25 less likely.
  - Using noise centred near 18 (sd 6.6), the chance of no trade is about 0.63 for each lower value and about 0.43 for 25.
  - That lowers P(25) to about 0.12 and leaves about 0.18 for each other value.
- Quote 8 (sale at 12.8): this tells me nothing about the value. 12.8 is below the minimum of 14, so only a noise trader would sell there.
- Updated fair value: 0.176 × (14 + 15 + 16 + 17 + 21) + 0.12 × 25 ≈ 17.6.

**Ask.** Expected profit = 0.8 × P(noise buys) × (ask − 17.6) + 0.2 × expected loss to informed buyers (when the value is above the ask).

| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 21 | ≈ 0.73 |
| 22 | ≈ 0.82 |
| 23 | ≈ 0.85 (best) |
| 24 | ≈ 0.83 |

**Bid.** Informed traders never sell at a bid below 14, so only noise matters here.

| Bid | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 13.9 | ≈ 0.85 |
| 13 | ≈ 0.89 |
| 12.5 to 12.6 | ≈ 0.90 (best) |
| 12 | ≈ 0.89 |

So I bid 12.6 and offer at 23.0.

{"bid": 12.6, "ask": 23.0}

game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Three dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (4 faces, each equally likely): 1, 5, 7, 10.
- Die 2 (6 faces, each equally likely): 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 12.
- Die 3 (8 faces, each equally likely): 0, 0, 1, 6, 6, 7, 11, 11.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
The fair value is the expected sum of the three dice: 5.75 + 5 + 5.25 = **16.0**.

**Uncertainty.** The variance is about 10.7 + 14.7 + 17.9 ≈ 43.3, so the standard deviation is about 6.6. That is roughly the same size as the noise traders' spread.

**Choosing the spread.** I compared, for each half-spread h, the expected profit from noise traders with the expected loss to informed traders:
- **h = 4:** about +0.65 per side.
- **h ≈ 5.3:** about +0.74 per side, the best of the three.
- **h ≈ 6.6:** about +0.73 per side.

So the best half-spread is about 5 to 5.5 on each side of 16.

{"bid": 10.8, "ask": 21.2}

Fair value is about 16, so I'm keeping a wide quote (half-spread about 5.5), similar to last time.

**Expected settlement value**
- Die 1: (1+5+7+10)/4 = 5.75
- Die 2: (1+2+3+4+8+12)/6 = 5.00
- Die 3: (0+0+1+6+6+7+11+11)/8 = 5.25
- Total: **16.0**

**Uncertainty**
- Variance of the sum ≈ 10.69 + 14.67 + 17.94 ≈ 43.3, so the standard deviation is about 6.6.
- That matches the noise traders' standard deviation of 6.6.

**Spread choice**
- I picked the half-spread h to maximise expected profit per side, approximating both the informed and noise valuations as Normal with σ ≈ 6.6.
- Expected profit per side is roughly σ·[x·Q(x) − 0.2·φ(x)], where x = h/σ, Q is the Normal upper-tail probability and φ is the Normal density.
- This is maximised where Q(x) = 0.8·x·φ(x), which gives x ≈ 0.85–0.9, so h ≈ 5.5–5.8.
- The distribution isn't truly Normal, so this is only a guide.
- Last quote's no-trade carries little information, so fair value stays at 16.

{"bid": 10.5, "ask": 21.5}

Fair value is 17.75, and I'm quoting 12.7 bid / 23.3 ask.

**Fair value.** With die 3 revealed as 7, fair value = E[die 1] + E[die 2] + 7 = 5.75 + 5 + 7 = 17.75.

**Remaining uncertainty.** Die 1 + die 2 has 24 equally likely outcomes. As deviations from fair value, they run from −8.75 to +11.25 and lean upward: the large outcomes are +11.25, +8.25 and +7.25.

**Choosing each half-spread.** For each side, I weighed the noise-trader profit against the expected loss to informed traders:
- Noise profit is 0.8 × half-spread × the chance a noise valuation falls outside my quote.
- Informed loss is 0.2 × the average amount by which the true value lands beyond my quote.

**Ask side.** Expected profit per quote by distance above fair value:

| Ask distance | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 4 | ≈ 0.73 |
| 5 | ≈ 0.79 |
| 5.5 | ≈ 0.80 |
| 6 | ≈ 0.80 |

I set the ask 5.5 above fair value, at 23.25, which rounds up to 23.3.

**Bid side.** Downside outcomes are smaller, so the bid can sit closer:

| Bid distance | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 4.5 | ≈ 0.80 |
| 5 | ≈ 0.82 |

I set the bid 5 below fair value, at 12.75, which rounds down to 12.7.

{"bid": 12.7, "ask": 23.3}

Die 3 is now known to be 7. That leaves the sum as die 1 plus die 2 plus 7.

**Fair value**
- Die 1 averages (1+5+7+10)/4 = 5.75.
- Die 2 averages (1+2+3+4+8+12)/6 = 5.
- The public fair value is 5.75 + 5 + 7 = **17.75**.
- No trades have happened so far, so the history doesn't move this estimate.

**What the settlement could be**
Die 1 and die 2 give 24 equally likely combinations. The possible settlements are:
- If die 1 = 1: 9, 10, 11, 12, 16, 20
- If die 1 = 5: 13, 14, 15, 16, 20, 24
- If die 1 = 7: 15, 16, 17, 18, 22, 26
- If die 1 = 10: 18, 19, 20, 21, 25, 29

**Choosing the quotes**
For each candidate price, I weighed two effects:
- **Loss to informed traders (20% chance):** they trade only when the true value is beyond my price, and I lose that gap.
- **Gain from noise traders (80% chance):** their valuations spread around 17.75 with standard deviation 6.6. I earn the distance from fair value times the chance they cross my price.

Net expected profit per quote:

| Side | Price | Net expected profit |
|---|---|---|
| Ask | 20.5 | 0.54 |
| Ask | 21.5 | 0.70 |
| Ask | 22.5 | 0.78 |
| Ask | 23 to 23.5 | about 0.80 (peak) |
| Bid | 13 | 0.81 |
| Bid | 12 to 12.5 | about 0.83 (peak) |

Both sides peak at about the same distance from fair value. So I'll quote a bid of 12.5 and an ask of 23.0.

{"bid": 12.5, "ask": 23.0}

Bid 11.5, ask 22.0, which centres the quote a bit below fair value of about 16.75 since I'm already long 1.

**Fair value**
- Before any trading, the expected sum is die 1 (5.75) + die 2 (5.0) + die 3 (7) = 17.75.
- Quote 4 had no trade at 12.7 / 23.3. That makes settlement values between 12.7 and 23.3 more likely, since an informed trader would only trade outside that range.
- At quote 5 someone sold to me at 12.5. That weights the low outcomes (9 to 12, which needs die 1 = 1 and die 2 of 4 or less). If the value is that low, the chance of a sell is about 0.37; otherwise it is about 0.17.
- Combining the 24 possible outcomes with these two pieces of evidence gives a fair value of about **16.75**.

**Bid**
- At 11.5, a noise trader sells to me about 20% of the time, with about 5.25 of edge per trade.
- Informed sellers would only hit it when the value is 9 to 11, and the loss there is small.
- Expected profit per quote is about 0.85. That is roughly the best among the bids I checked (11.0 to 13.0).

**Ask**
- At 22.0, a noise trader buys about 21% of the time, with about 5.25 of edge per trade.
- Informed buyers would only take it at values 24, 25, 26 or 29, which have about an 11% chance combined.
- Expected profit per quote is about 0.81. That is better than asks at 21 or 21.5.

{"bid": 11.5, "ask": 22.0}

Die 1 (5) plus die 3 (7) gives 12, so the settlement is 12 plus die 2. Die 2 is one of {1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 12}, which puts the settlement at 13, 14, 15, 16, 20 or 24. The prior mean is 17.

**Updating on the trading history:**
- At quotes 4 and 6 an informed trader with value 24 would have bought at my ask. Neither quote traded, which roughly halves the weight on die 2 = 12.
- The sale at 12.5 tells us nothing about die 2. No possible value is below 12.5, so that seller must have been a noise trader.
- The posterior mean of die 2 is about 4.35, so public fair value is about 16.35.

**Choosing the quotes:**
- **Ask:** I traded off the edge earned from noise buyers against losses to informed buyers when the value is 20 or 24. Expected profit is highest for an ask between about 21 and 22. Selling would also flatten my long position.
- **Bid:** Informed traders cannot sell profitably below 13. Below that, expected profit is fairly flat between 11.5 and 12.

{"bid": 11.8, "ask": 21.5}

Die 1 and die 3 are revealed, so their sum is 5 + 7 = 12. The settlement value is 12 + die 2, which can be 13, 14, 15, 16, 20 or 24.

**What the trades so far tell us**
- **Sell at 12.5 (quote 5):** with die 1 = 5, an informed trader would never sell at 12.5, because the lowest possible value is 13. So that trade came from a noise trader and says nothing about die 2.
- **No trade at 11.8 / 21.5 (quote 7):** if die 2 were 12 (value 24), an informed trader would have bought at 21.5. The lack of a trade makes value 24 a bit less likely.
- **Posterior on value:** about 0.12 for 24 and about 0.176 for each of the other five values.
- **Public fair value:** about 16.6.

**Ask**
- An ask at 20 or above means informed traders only buy when the value is 24.
- Expected profit (noise gains minus informed losses) is highest near 22:

| Ask | Noise gain | Informed loss | Net |
|---|---|---|---|
| 21 | 0.89 | 0.07 | 0.82 |
| 22 | 0.89 | 0.05 | 0.85 |
| 23 | 0.85 | 0.02 | 0.83 |

**Bid**
- A bid below 13 means informed traders never sell to me, so only noise traders matter.
- The expected gain from noise sells is about 0.84 at a bid of 13, 0.89 at 12 and 0.89 at 11. The best bid is around 12.

{"bid": 12.0, "ask": 22.0}

With one quote left, I priced the contract on what is known so far and on what the trade history implies about die 2.

**Fair value**
- Die 3 = 7 and die 1 = 5, so the settlement value is 12 plus die 2. That gives possible values of 13, 14, 15, 16, 20 or 24.
- The two sells at my bid (12.5 and 12) must have come from noise traders. Every possible value is at least 13, so an informed trader would never sell that low.
- The no-trade quotes at 4, 6 and 7 count against die 2 = 12. An informed trader holding a value of 24 would have bought at my asks of 23.3, 22 and 21.5.
- At each of those quotes, a noise trader had about a 57% chance of not trading. Combining the three gives a likelihood ratio of about 0.33 for the value 24.
- The other five values keep weights of about 0.19 each, and 24 falls to about 0.06. The posterior fair value is about **16.1**.

**Choosing the quote**
- For each candidate price I added the expected profit from noise trades to the expected loss to informed traders.
- **Ask:** around 21 is best. At 21 I lose to informed traders only when the value is 24, and noise buyers still trade with me about 23% of the time.
- **Bid:** around 11 is best. Informed traders never sell below 13, so the only question is how much noise selling I give up by bidding lower.

Total expected profit is roughly flat near both optima, so I post a bid of 11.2 and an ask of 21.3.

{"bid": 11.2, "ask": 21.3}

game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Three dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (8 faces, each equally likely): 3, 6, 7, 8, 8, 10, 11, 11.
- Die 2 (6 faces, each equally likely): 0, 2, 4, 8, 8, 10.
- Die 3 (8 faces, each equally likely): 0, 1, 6, 8, 8, 9, 10, 10.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
The settlement value is the sum of the three dice, so the starting fair value is the sum of the three die averages.

**Fair value**
- Die 1 averages 64/8 = 8.0.
- Die 2 averages 32/6 ≈ 5.33.
- Die 3 averages 52/8 = 6.5.
- Fair value ≈ 8.0 + 5.33 + 6.5 = 19.83.

**Uncertainty**
- The die variances are about 6.5, 12.9 and 13.5, so the total variance is about 32.9.
- The standard deviation of the sum is about 5.74, roughly the same as the noise traders' 5.7.

**Spread choice**
- Treat the settlement value as roughly Normal and write the half-spread h as x standard deviations.
- Expected profit per side is then about s·[x·Q(x) − 0.35·φ(x)], where Q is the upper-tail probability and φ the Normal density. The first term is the gain from noise traders; the second is the expected loss to informed traders.
- This is largest where Q(x) = 0.65·x·φ(x), which gives x ≈ 1.
- In price terms, that is a half-spread of about 5.5 to 5.7.

So I quote a bid of 14.3 and an ask of 25.4, about 5.5 either side of fair value.

{"bid": 14.3, "ask": 25.4}

Fair value is about 22.33. That is die 3 at 9, plus 8 expected from die 1, plus about 5.33 expected from die 2.

I checked half-spreads against the actual distribution of die 1 + die 2:
- **Ask side:** profit from noise traders minus losses to informed traders peaks at a half-spread of about 5 to 6. The net is about 0.55 per quote.
- **Bid side:** the lower tail is similar and also peaks at about 5 to 6.

So I quote about 5.5 either side of fair.

{"bid": 16.8, "ask": 27.8}

Die 3 = 9, so before the trade the fair value was 8 (die 1) + 5.33 (die 2) + 9 = 22.33.

**Update from the buy at 27.8**
- An informed buyer means die 1 + die 2 ≥ 19. That is 7 of the 48 equally likely combinations.
- A noise trader buys at 27.8 with probability about 0.17.
- Weighting each combination by how likely it was to produce that buy gives a posterior mean for die 1 + die 2 of about 15.36. The fair value is now about 24.4.

**Choosing the ask**
- The highest possible settlement value is 30, so an ask of 30.0 can never be lifted by an informed trader.
- Its expected edge from noise traders is about 0.59 per quote, which is about the best of the asks I checked.

**Choosing the bid**
- I set the bid to balance noise-trader edge against informed sellers when the value is low.
- A bid near 19 maximises expected profit at about 0.46 per quote.

{"bid": 19.0, "ask": 30.0}

With die 3 = 9 and die 1 = 10 revealed, the known part of the sum is 19. Die 2 is still hidden.

**Possible outcomes**
- Die 2 can be 0, 2, 4, 8, 8 or 10, each equally likely.
- So settlement is 19, 21, 23, 27, 27 or 29.
- The expected value of die 2 is 32 / 6 ≈ 5.33, so public fair value is about 24.33.

**Ask side**
- At 29.1 an informed trader never buys, because settlement cannot exceed 29.
- A noise trader buys with probability of about 0.20, for an edge of about 4.77.
- Expected value is about +0.62.
- Lowering the ask to 27.1 lets informed traders buy whenever die 2 is 8 or 10. That drops the expected value to about +0.47.

**Bid side**
- At 18.9 an informed trader never sells, because settlement cannot be below 19.
- A noise trader sells with probability of about 0.17, for an edge of about 5.43.
- Expected value is about +0.60.
- Raising the bid to 20.9 gets hit by informed traders when settlement is 19. That drops the expected value to about +0.50.

A position change of one unit stays well within the limits.

{"bid": 18.9, "ask": 29.1}

The last quote is a single exposure, so I chose each side's price to maximise expected profit.

**Public fair value.** Die 3 is 9 and die 1 is 10, so 19 is known. Die 2 averages (0+2+4+8+8+10)/6 = 5.33. That gives an expected settlement of about 24.33. The possible settlements are 19, 21, 23, 27, 27 and 29, each with probability 1/6. Quote 5 traded nothing, so the trading history adds almost no information.

**Ask side.**
- At an ask of 29.0, no informed trader buys, because the value is never above 29.
- A noise trader buys with probability P(N > 4.67/5.7) ≈ 0.21.
- Expected profit ≈ 0.65 × 0.21 × 4.67 ≈ 0.62.
- Lower asks did worse: 28 gives about 0.56 and 26.9 about 0.41, because informed buyers start picking me off.

**Bid side.**
- At a bid of 19.0, no informed trader sells, because the value is never below 19.
- A noise trader sells with probability P(N < −5.33/5.7) ≈ 0.175.
- Expected profit ≈ 0.65 × 0.175 × 5.33 ≈ 0.61.
- Higher bids did worse: 19.5 gives about 0.59, 21 about 0.49, and 23 about 0.

Both sides are safe from informed traders at these prices, and each earns about 0.6 from noise traders.

{"bid": 19.0, "ask": 29.0}

game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Two dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (4 faces, each equally likely): 0, 3, 10, 11.
- Die 2 (6 faces, each equally likely): 0, 6, 7, 11, 12, 12.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
Fair value is 14 (die 1 averages 6, die 2 averages 8). The sum has a standard deviation of about 6.3.

I weighed the profit from noise traders (noise SD 4.7) against losses to informed traders (20%) at different widths. The best width is about ±4 to ±5 on each side, each worth about +0.42 per quote.

- **Ask at 18.5:** informed traders buy only when the sum is 21 or more. I earn 4.5 from noise buyers about 17% of the time.
- **Bid at 9.5:** informed traders sell only when the sum is 9 or less, with a similar trade-off.

{"bid": 9.5, "ask": 18.5}

The prior expected sum is 6 (die 1) + 8 (die 2) = 14. Someone sold at my 9.5 bid, which is evidence the value is low. Weighting the outcomes for that sale moves fair value to about **11.9**.

I compared expected edge per quote for several prices. At each price this is the profit from noise traders minus the losses to informed traders:

- **Ask:** about 0.31 at 15, 0.37 at 16 and 0.36 at 17. The best is around 16.
- **Bid:** about 0.38 at 8 and 0.39 at 7, so the best is roughly 7 to 8.

My position is +1 long, so inventory is not a constraint. I'll bid 7.5 and ask 16.

  - It is about 0.06 for any other face.
- **Posterior:** P(die 1 = 8) ≈ 0.57. Fair value ≈ 0.57×18 + 0.43×(10 + 4.57) ≈ 16.5.
- **Quote 2 (no trade at 7 / 18.3):** This tells us nothing more about die 1, since every possible value lies inside that spread.

**Ask:** The highest possible value is 18, so an informed trader never buys at an ask of 18 or more. Above that, only noise traders buy. Expected profit per quote is (ask − 16.5) × 0.5 × P(noise valuation > ask), which peaks near an ask of about 20.

info.raw:
Before any cards are shown, the fair value is 21 (three cards averaging 7). The sum's standard deviation is about 6.35, close to the noise traders' 6.4.

**Choosing the spread.** Treat both trader types as roughly normal around 21 with standard deviation σ ≈ 6.4, and quote 21 ± s. Write x = s/σ, φ for the standard normal density and Φ for its cumulative distribution.
- The gain from noise traders is about s·(1−Φ(x)).
- The loss to informed traders is about σ[φ(x) − x(1−Φ(x))].
- Combining both and putting x in place of s/σ, the expected profit per side is about 0.5σ[2x(1−Φ(x)) − φ(x)].
- That expression peaks near x ≈ 1.2, so s ≈ 7.7.

This gives a bid of 21 − 7.7 = 13.3 and an ask of 21 + 7.7 = 28.7.

{"bid": 13.3, "ask": 28.7}

- **Choosing the half-spread:** For each half-spread, I weighed profit from noise traders against expected losses to informed traders.
  - About 4 nets roughly 0.20 per side.
  - About 5 nets roughly 0.31.
  - About 6 nets roughly 0.36.
  - About 7 nets roughly 0.37.
- **Result:** Expected profit is flat between 6 and 7.5.

{"bid": 14.2, "ask": 27.8}

To set the half-spread d, I compare two effects on each side:
- **Noise traders:** they pay me d per trade and trade with probability P(noise > d), where the noise standard deviation is 6.4.
- **Informed traders:** they cost me E[(V − ask)+], the expected amount by which the true value V exceeds my ask when they buy.

Checking a few half-spreads gives these net gains per unit before the 0.5 weighting:

| d | Net |
|---|---|
| 5 | 0.61 |
| 6 | 0.71 |
| 7 | 0.74 |
| 8 | 0.70 |

The best is d ≈ 7, so I quote about 22.9 ± 7.

{"bid": 15.9, "ask": 29.9}

Fair value is about 22.9. Card 1 is a 9, so the other 51 cards sum to 364 − 9 = 355, an average of 6.96 per card. The two unseen cards should add about 13.92, giving 9 + 13.92 ≈ 22.9.

| 4 | 0.20 |

The best range is about 6.5 to 7, so I quote roughly 22.9 ± 6.7.

  - A noise trader would have sold with roughly a 15% chance whatever card 3 is.
- Updating on that sale, there is about a 60% chance card 3 is 1 or 2, giving a sum of 15 or 16.
- In the other 40%, card 3 averages about 8.05, giving a sum spread from 17 to 27.

**Bid**
- The lowest possible sum is 15, so any bid below 15 is never hit by an informed trader.
- Noise traders will still sell below 15. Expected profit is flat at about 0.5 to 0.54 per quote for bids between 13 and 15.

**Ask**

| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 23 | about 0.35 |
| 25 | about 0.42 |
| 26 | about 0.41 |
| 27 | about 0.37 |

With card 1 = 9 and card 2 = 5 revealed, the settlement is 14 plus card 3.

- **Bid.** At 15.0, no informed trader can sell below it, since the minimum value is 15. A noise seller below 15 earns me about 6.1 per trade. Bidding 16.0 would lose 1 to an informed seller holding 15, which costs more than the extra noise flow gains.
- **Ask.** At 27.0, no informed trader buys, since the maximum value is 27. Noise buyers above 27 pay me about 5.9 over fair value. Asking 26.0 would lose 1 to an informed buyer holding 27.
