- Expected bias E[p] ≈ 0.560, so the 2 remaining flips add about 1.12 expected heads.
- Settlement distribution: 3 with probability ≈ 0.21, 4 with ≈ 0.46, 5 with ≈ 0.33. The mean is about 4.12.
- The buy at 5.9 tells us nothing. The maximum settlement is 5, so an informed trader would never buy at 5.9. That trade must have come from a noise trader.

**Ask.** If the ask is above 5, informed traders never buy, so I only trade with noise traders. Expected profit at each ask level:

| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 5.5 | ≈ 0.336 |
| 6.0 | ≈ 0.366 |
| 6.5 | ≈ 0.360 |

**Bid.** If the bid is below 3, informed traders never sell, because the settlement is at least 3.

| Bid | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 3.0 | ≈ 0.30 |
| 2.5 | ≈ 0.355 |
| 2.0–2.2 | ≈ 0.367 |

There is one unit of room before the +3 position limit, so I can still bid.

{"bid": 2.1, "ask": 6.1}

With 3 heads in 5 revealed flips, the coin is most likely fair or biased toward heads. That puts fair value near 4.12, and I'll quote about 2 points either side.

**Probability of each coin given the flips**

| P(heads) | Prior × likelihood of 3 heads, 2 tails | Posterior |
|---|---|---|
| 0.2 | 0.3 × 0.00512 = 0.00154 | 0.066 |
| 0.5 | 0.4 × 0.03125 = 0.01250 | 0.537 |
| 0.7 | 0.3 × 0.03087 = 0.00926 | 0.398 |

- **Expected P(heads)** is about 0.56. Flips 6 and 7 add about 1.12 expected heads.
- **Fair value** is 3 + 1.12 ≈ **4.12**.
- **Settlement** is 3, 4 or 5, with probabilities of about 0.21, 0.46 and 0.33.

**Choosing the quotes**

- **Ask:** An ask above 5 can never lose to an informed buyer. Above that, expected profit from noise traders is 0.8 × (a − 4.12) × P(noise > a − 4.12). With a standard deviation of 2.7, this is highest at about a − 4.12 ≈ 2.0, so the ask is about **6.1**. That gives about +0.37 expected profit. An ask just under 5 is worse because the informed trader buys whenever settlement is 5.
- **Bid:** The same reasoning on the other side gives a bid below 3 at about **2.1**, so an informed seller never trades against it.
- **Position:** Both sides are allowed, since I am at +2. Inventory does not change expected profit, so I keep the quotes symmetric.

{"bid": 2.1, "ask": 6.1}

game.title: Coin of unknown bias
game.description: A coin is picked at random from a set of coins: P(heads) = 0.3 with probability 1/5, P(heads) = 0.4 with probability 3/10, P(heads) = 0.5 with probability 1/2. The coin is not shown. It is flipped 6 times. Revealed flips show 1 for heads and 0 for tails.
game.contract: The contract settles at the number of heads in all flips.

info.raw:
The expected settlement is about 2.58, and I'm quoting bid 1.0 and ask 4.0.

**Fair value.** The coin's expected heads probability is 0.2×0.3 + 0.3×0.4 + 0.5×0.5 = 0.43. Over 6 flips that gives 6 × 0.43 ≈ 2.58 expected heads, with a standard deviation of about 1.29.

**Informed traders.** The settlement is a whole number, so I put my quotes exactly on integers.
- An ask of 4.0 means an informed trader buys only if the settlement is 5 or 6. That happens about 6–8% of the time.
- A bid of 1.0 means an informed trader sells only if the settlement is 0. That happens about 4% of the time.
- Expected loss to informed traders is roughly 0.06 per quote.

**Noise traders.** Their valuations are spread around 2.58 with a standard deviation of 1.3.
- They buy at 4.0 about 14% of the time, and I gain about 1.42 each time.
- They sell at 1.0 about 11% of the time, and I gain about 1.58 each time.
- Expected gain from noise traders is roughly 0.19 per quote.

**Why not tighter.** I also checked a 2.0/3.0 quote. Informed traders would then trade when the settlement is 4 or more, or 1 or less, which is much more often. The expected profit came out slightly negative, so the wider quote is better.

{"bid": 1.0, "ask": 4.0}

The settlement value is the number of heads in 6 flips, with no flips revealed yet.

**Fair value and spread**
- Expected chance of heads per flip: 0.2·0.3 + 0.3·0.4 + 0.5·0.5 = 0.43.
- Fair value is 6 × 0.43 = 2.58 heads.
- The settlement value has a standard deviation of about 1.29.

**Settlement distribution (mix of the three coins)**

| Heads | 0 | 1 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | ≈0.045 | ≈0.163 | ≈0.171 | ≈0.060 | ≈0.009 |

**Ask side**
- An informed trader values the contract at a whole number, so asks between whole numbers mainly change what I earn from noise traders.
- An ask of 3.1 loses money: informed buyers whenever the value is 4 or more cost more than noise buyers pay.
- An ask around 4.0 gains about +0.058 per quote. Informed traders buy only when the value is 5 or more, and noise traders who buy pay about 1.42 above fair value.

**Bid side**
- A bid of 2.0 or 1.9 loses money because informed traders sell whenever the value is 0 or 1.
- Bids from 1.0 to 1.5 gain money; the best is a bid of about 1.4, worth roughly +0.076 per quote.

{"bid": 1.4, "ask": 4.0}

Fair value is about 2.6, and I'll quote bid 1.0 and ask 4.0.

**Fair value.**
- **Coin after the revealed head:** the chance of each coin shifts to about 0.14 (P=0.3), 0.28 (P=0.4) and 0.58 (P=0.5). The expected P(heads) is about 0.444.
- **Without the trading history:** expected heads would be 1 + 5 × 0.444 ≈ 3.2.
- **What the trading history adds:** someone sold to me at 1.4 in stage 1. An informed seller would only do that if the total is at most 1. Since flip 1 was a head, that means flips 2–6 are all tails.
  - Updating on that sale and the earlier no-trade puts about a 30% chance on exactly 1 head.
  - The other 70% sits around 3.4 heads.
  - Combined, the public fair value is about 2.6.

**Bid.** An informed seller only gains if the true total is below my bid, and the total cannot be below 1. So a bid of 1.0 loses nothing to informed traders. It still collects some noise traders who value the contract below 1. Raising the bid lets informed traders with a total of 1 sell to me, and that costs more than it earns.

**Ask.** I compared expected profit per quote for several asks:

| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 3.0 | about −0.13 |
| 3.5 | about −0.02 |
| 3.9 | about +0.04 |
| 4.0 | about +0.045 |
| 4.2 | about +0.045 |

Asks of 4.0 to 4.2 do best because only totals of 5 or 6 heads make an informed buyer take them. I'll use 4.0.

{"bid": 1.0, "ask": 4.0}

I value the contract at about **2.4**, and I'll quote a bid of 1.0 and an ask of 4.0.

**Fair value.** Settlement S = 1 + K, where K is the number of heads in flips 2–6.

- After seeing flip 1 = heads, the coin probabilities shift. P(heads) = 0.3, 0.4 and 0.5 become about 0.14, 0.28 and 0.58.
- The trading history also tells us something, mainly the counterparty who sold at 1.4 in quote 2.
  - An informed seller there means S ≤ 1, so K = 0.
  - A noise trader would only have sold that low with probability about 0.18.
- The two no-trade quotes add a smaller adjustment.

Weighting the possible values of K by both the coin and the trades gives roughly:

| K | Probability |
|---|---|
| 0 | 0.33 |
| 1 | 0.17 |
| 2 | 0.26 |
| 3 | 0.21 |
| 4 or more | 0.02 |

That puts the expected settlement at about 2.4.

**Choosing the quotes.**
- **Bid:** 1.0 is best. An informed trader can't sell profitably to me, since S is at least 1. Noise sellers still give a small positive edge.
- **Ask:** 4.0 is best. Informed buyers only profit when S ≥ 5, which has only about a 2% chance. Noise buyers above 4 give a positive edge.
- **Position:** I'm long 1, so I'm happy for the ask to get hit.

{"bid": 1.0, "ask": 4.0}

Five flips are revealed with 2 heads, so the contract settles at either 2 or 3. It depends only on flip 6.

**Fair value**

The posterior on the coin, using the likelihood p²(1−p)³ times the prior:
- p = 0.3: 0.00617
- p = 0.4: 0.01037
- p = 0.5: 0.01563

This gives P(flip 6 = heads) ≈ 0.43, so the fair value is about 2.43.

The sale at 1.4 in quote 2 must have come from a noise trader. An informed seller would know the value is at least 2 and would not sell at 1.4. So the trade tells us nothing more.

**Quoting**

- **Bid 2.0:** An informed trader only sells if the value is below my bid. Since the value is at least 2, no informed trader sells to me here. A noise trader sells with probability about 37%, and I gain about 0.43 when that happens. Raising the bid to 2.1 would let informed traders with value 2 sell to me, which lowers my expected profit.
- **Ask 3.0:** An informed trader with value 3 does not buy, because 3 is not above 3. A noise trader buys with probability about 33%, and I gain about 0.57. Lowering the ask to 2.9 would invite informed buyers.

My position stays within limits either way.

{"bid": 2.0, "ask": 3.0}

The settlement value must be 2 or 3: two heads so far, plus flip 6. The quote is set to profit from noise traders while giving informed traders no reason to trade.

**Coin posterior** (after 2 heads and 3 tails):

| Coin P(heads) | Prior × p²(1−p)³ | Posterior |
|---|---|---|
| 0.3 | 0.2 × 0.03087 = 0.00617 | ≈ 0.19 |
| 0.4 | 0.3 × 0.03456 = 0.01037 | ≈ 0.32 |
| 0.5 | 0.5 × 0.03125 = 0.01563 | ≈ 0.49 |

- The chance flip 6 is heads is about 0.429, so fair value is about 2.43.
- The trading history adds no information. Both sales were at bids that an informed trader would never hit, given that the value is at least 2.

**Informed traders:**
- At any bid of 2.0 or lower, an informed trader never sells, because their value is at least 2.
- At any ask of 3.0 or higher, an informed trader never buys, because their value is at most 3.
- Within those limits, only noise traders reach me. Their valuations are normally distributed around 2.43 with standard deviation 1.3.

**Optimal distance from fair value:** The expected profit on each side is x · P(noise valuation crosses the quote), where x is the distance from fair value. This is largest at x ≈ 0.75 × 1.3 ≈ 0.98.

- **Ask** ≈ 2.43 + 0.98 = 3.41. Rounding up gives 3.4, which is above 3, so it is safe from informed traders.
- **Bid** ≈ 2.43 − 0.98 = 1.45. A bid of 1.5 or 1.4 gives about the same expected profit (about 0.221 per noise trader). I choose 1.5, which is below 2, so it is safe from informed traders.

Buying at 1.5 would take my position to +3, which is within the +4 limit.

{"bid": 1.5, "ask": 3.4}

game.title: Coin of unknown bias
game.description: A coin is picked at random from a set of coins: P(heads) = 0.5 with probability 2/5, P(heads) = 0.7 with probability 3/5. The coin is not shown. It is flipped 7 times. Revealed flips show 1 for heads and 0 for tails.
game.contract: The contract settles at 10 times the number of heads in all flips.

info.raw:
Before any flips are shown, the fair value is about 43.4, but the settlement value could easily land 14 points either way. Informed traders are costly here because they know the exact outcome. So the best expected profit comes from a wide, slightly skewed quote.

**Fair value**
- The expected chance of heads is 0.4 × 0.5 + 0.6 × 0.7 = 0.62.
- Expected heads over 7 flips are 7 × 0.62 = 4.34, so the contract is worth about 43.4.
- The standard deviation of the settlement is about 14.3. That counts both the coin-flip randomness and not knowing which coin it is.

**Settlement distribution** (mixing the two coins):

| Value | 0 | 10 | 20 | 30 | 40 | 50 | 60 | 70 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 0.003 | 0.024 | 0.081 | 0.168 | 0.246 | 0.256 | 0.170 | 0.053 |

**Ask side**
Each quote's expected profit is the edge earned from noise traders (65%) minus the loss to informed traders (35%).
- An ask of 47 loses about 0.6 per quote.
- An ask of 50 makes about +0.2.
- Asks from 55 to 60 make about +0.53, which is the best range. I chose 56, worth about +0.54.

**Bid side**
- A bid of 40 loses about 0.6.
- A bid of 33 makes about +0.39.
- A bid of 30 makes about +0.50, the best I found. At exactly 30, an informed trader whose value is 30 does not sell, so I lose nothing in that case.

The quote is skewed upward because the distribution leans toward higher values.

{"bid": 30, "ask": 56}

Before any flips are revealed, the expected chance of heads is 0.4×0.5 + 0.6×0.7 = 0.62. That gives an expected 4.34 heads, so fair value is about 43.4. The settlement standard deviation is about 14. The last quote produced no trade, which tells us almost nothing.

I weighed the expected loss to informed traders against the expected gain from noise traders (noise sd 11) at different quote levels:
- **Ask:** expected profit is flat and highest at roughly 55–60.
- **Bid:** expected profit is highest at about 30, because the settlement value is skewed to the upside.

So I keep the same quote.

{"bid": 30, "ask": 56}

Posterior after flips 0, 1, 1: the 0.7 coin explains these flips better (likelihood 0.147 vs 0.125). That moves its probability from 0.6 to about 0.64. Expected P(heads) is then about 0.628.

Expected settlement is 10 × (2 + 4 × 0.628) ≈ 45.1. The earlier buy at 56 is mild evidence that the value is high, so I treat fair as about 45–46.

Settlement can only be a multiple of 10. With a bid of 40, an informed trader sells to me only if the value is 20 or 30. With an ask of 50, an informed trader buys from me only if the value is 60. Noise traders centred near 45 will still trade on both sides. Being short 1 is a small risk, so I quote around fair without skewing.

{"bid": 40, "ask": 50}

Fair value is about 50, and I'm quoting wide (bid 46, ask 58) because of the two buys and my short position.

**Fair value from the revealed flips (0, 1, 1)**
- The chance of seeing these flips is 0.125 for the 0.5 coin and 0.147 for the 0.7 coin.
- That gives P(coin is 0.7) ≈ 0.64, so the expected heads rate is about 0.628.
- With 2 heads so far and 4 flips left, the expected total is 2 + 2.51 ≈ 4.5 heads, or about 45.

**What the trading history suggests**
- Both counterparties bought, at 56 in stage 1 and at 50 in stage 2.
- An informed trader buys at those prices only if the settlement is above them. Given the flips so far, that means all 4 remaining flips are heads, a settlement of 60.
- Each buy therefore shifts weight toward 60. Updating on both buys moves fair value somewhere into the high 40s to mid 50s, depending on how much weight the buys get.

**My position**
- I'm short 2, so a settlement of 60 is my main risk. I don't want to sell much below 60.
- On the other side, informed traders sell to me only when the settlement is 50 or less. My bid should stay low enough that I'm not buying from them at a loss.

So I'm quoting a wide market skewed upward.

{"bid": 46, "ask": 58}

Fair value is about 49.3, so I'm quoting a bid of 40 and an ask of 60 to avoid being picked off by informed traders.

**Posterior on the coin** after 3 heads and 1 tail:
- Fair coin (p=0.5): 0.4 × 0.5⁴ = 0.0250
- Biased coin (p=0.7): 0.6 × 0.7³ × 0.3 = 0.0617
- So P(biased coin) ≈ 0.712, and the expected chance of heads on each remaining flip is about 0.642.

**Settlement distribution** (3 heads so far, 3 flips left):

| Settlement | 30 | 40 | 50 | 60 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 0.055 | 0.243 | 0.422 | 0.280 |

Public fair value ≈ 30 + 10 × 3 × 0.642 ≈ 49.3.

**Choosing the quotes:** Settlement can only be 30, 40, 50 or 60. Any ask strictly between 50 and 60 sells to informed traders whenever settlement is 60. Any bid between 40 and 50 buys from informed traders whenever settlement is 30 or 40.

- **Ask:** quoting at 60 avoids informed losses entirely. It still earns about +1.14 per quote from noise traders, who buy about 16% of the time with an edge of about 10.7.
- **Bid:** quoting at 40 only loses to informed traders when settlement is 30. Expected value is about +1.0 per quote; quotes closer to 50 lose money.

{"bid": 40, "ask": 60}

I'm quoting bid 45 and ask 55: centred on a fair value of about 49.3, with the bid skewed up because I'm short 2.

**Which coin it is.** The revealed flips are 0, 1, 1, 1, so 3 heads and 1 tail.
- Fair coin (0.5): prior 2/5 × likelihood 0.0625 = 0.025.
- Biased coin (0.7): prior 3/5 × likelihood 0.1029 = 0.0617.
- So P(biased coin) ≈ 0.71, and the expected P(heads) ≈ 0.642.

**Settlement distribution.** We have 3 heads so far and 3 flips left (5, 6 and 7).

| Settlement | Probability |
|---|---|
| 30 | 0.055 |
| 40 | 0.243 |
| 50 | 0.422 |
| 60 | 0.280 |

The expected settlement is about 49.3. Earlier buys at 56 and 50 suggest the value may be a little higher than this.

**Choosing the quote.**
- An ask of 55 is lifted by informed traders only when settlement is 60 (probability 0.28). It also earns spread from noise buyers.
- A bid of 45 is hit by informed traders when settlement is 30 or 40 (probability 0.30). Raising the bid slightly makes it more likely we buy back toward flat.

{"bid": 45, "ask": 55}

Six flips are revealed and 5 of them are heads, so the coin is probably the 0.7 coin.

**Posterior on the coin**
- Chance of 5 heads in 6 flips (one particular order) with the fair coin: 0.5⁶ ≈ 0.0156.
- Same with the biased coin: 0.7⁵ × 0.3 ≈ 0.0504.
- Weighting by the priors: 0.4 × 0.0156 = 0.00625 and 0.6 × 0.0504 = 0.03025.
- So P(biased coin) ≈ 0.829.

**Settlement**
- P(flip 7 is heads) = 0.171 × 0.5 + 0.829 × 0.7 ≈ 0.666.
- The contract settles at either 50 or 60.
- Fair value ≈ 56.7.

**Quote choice**
- The informed trader only trades against me if my bid is above 50 or my ask is below 60.
- So I keep the bid at or below 50 and the ask at or above 60, and set each side to maximise expected profit from noise traders.
- On the ask side, expected profit is about 1.09 at 62, 1.20 at 64 and 1.20 at 66, so it peaks around 64–66.
- On the bid side, expected profit is about 1.18 at 50, 1.21 at 48 and 1.19 at 47, so anywhere from 48 to 50 works.
- My short position of 3 is small enough to tolerate.

I'll quote a bid of 49 and an ask of 65.

{"bid": 49, "ask": 65}

This is the last quote and I'm at -3, so position limits don't constrain me. I set each side to maximise its expected profit on its own terms.

**Fair value**
- Revealed flips show 5 heads in 6.
- The chance of exactly this sequence is 0.5⁶ = 0.0156 for the fair coin and 0.7⁵·0.3 = 0.0504 for the 0.7 coin.
- Weighting by the priors (2/5 and 3/5), the posterior P(coin = 0.7) is about 0.829.
- P(flip 7 = heads) = 0.171·0.5 + 0.829·0.7 ≈ 0.666.
- The contract settles at 50 or 60, so fair value ≈ 56.66.

**Ask side**
- Any ask below 60 is bought by an informed trader whenever settlement is 60, which loses money.
- At 60 or above, only noise traders trade, with valuations Normal(56.66, 11).
- Expected profit is roughly 0.65 · x · P(Z > x/11), where x is the ask minus 56.66. This is largest at about x = 0.75·11 ≈ 8.3.
- That gives an ask of about 65, worth about 1.2 in expected profit. An ask of exactly 60 would earn only about 0.83.

**Bid side**
- Any bid above 50 is hit by an informed trader whenever settlement is 50.
- At or below 50, the same calculation gives an optimum about 8.3 below fair value, so a bid near 48.4.
- I'll bid 48.5, which earns about 1.2 in expected profit.

{"bid": 48.5, "ask": 65}

game.title: Coin of unknown bias
game.description: A coin is picked at random from a set of coins: P(heads) = 0.5 with probability 2/5, P(heads) = 0.7 with probability 3/5. The coin is not shown. It is flipped 7 times. Revealed flips show 1 for heads and 0 for tails.
game.contract: The contract settles at 10 times the number of heads in all flips.

info.raw:
The contract is worth about 43.4 in expectation, and I'm quoting a wide market around that: bid 30, ask 56.5.

**Fair value**
- The expected chance of heads is 0.4×0.5 + 0.6×0.7 = 0.62.
- Over 7 flips that gives 4.34 expected heads, so the contract is worth about 43.4.
- The settlement value has a standard deviation of about 14. That is wider than the noise traders' spread of 11, so informed traders are a large risk.

**Settlement distribution (number of heads, from the 0.5/0.7 mixture)**

| Heads | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 0.003 | 0.024 | 0.081 | 0.168 | 0.246 | 0.256 | 0.170 | 0.053 |

**Choosing the ask**
For each candidate price I weighed what I make from noise traders against what I lose to informed traders.
- An ask just above 50 earns about +0.2 per quote.
- An ask around 55–58 earns about +0.53.
- An ask near 56.5 is close to the best, at about +0.54.

**Choosing the bid**
- A bid near 30 earns about +0.49 per quote.
- A higher bid, such as 39.9, loses heavily to informed sellers when the value is 30 or less.

{"bid": 30.0, "ask": 56.5}

Quoting bid 30, ask 57, wider below fair than above, because the settlement odds are lopsided.

**Fair value.** The expected chance of heads is 0.4×0.5 + 0.6×0.7 = 0.62. Over 7 flips that gives an expected value of 7 × 0.62 × 10 = 43.4. The standard deviation is about 14. Settlement can only land on multiples of 10. The lack of a trade at quote 1 tells me very little.

**Ask side.**
- Informed buyers only hurt me when the value is 60 or more. That has a probability of about 0.22: 60 is about 0.17 and 70 is about 0.05.
- Noise buyers trade with me when their valuation is above my ask. Their valuations are spread around 43.4 with a standard deviation of 11.
- Expected profit per quote is about +0.53 at an ask of 55 and also at 58. So the best ask is around 56–57, just under 60.

**Bid side.**
- Informed sellers only hurt me when the value is 30 or less. Rough probabilities are 30 at about 0.17, 20 at about 0.08, and 10 or below at about 0.03.
- Expected profit is about +0.40 at a bid of 33, +0.49 at 30 and +0.40 at 28. So the best bid is around 30.

{"bid": 30, "ask": 57}

**Fair value after three heads**
- The chance the coin is the 0.7 coin rises to about 0.80.
- Each remaining flip is then heads with probability about 0.66.
- Expected settlement is 10 × (3 + 4 × 0.661), which is about **56.4**.

**Possible settlement values**
With 4 flips left, settlement can only be 30, 40, 50, 60 or 70. Their probabilities are about 0.02, 0.11, 0.29, 0.38 and 0.21.

**Choosing the quote**
An informed trader only hurts me when the true value crosses my price. Because the value can only land on multiples of 10, I can set my prices to limit those losses.

| Side | Price | Expected loss to informed | Expected gain from noise | Net expected edge |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ask | 60.1 | 0.71 | 0.89 | +0.17 |
| Ask | 67 | — | — | +0.94 |
| Ask | 68 | 0.14 | 1.11 | **+0.97** (best) |
| Ask | 69 | — | — | +0.96 |
| Bid | 49.9 | — | — | +0.66 |
| Bid | 45 | — | — | +0.82 |
| Bid | 46 | 0.34 | 1.17 | **+0.83** (best) |
| Bid | 47 | — | — | +0.82 |

- **Ask:** at 60.1 an informed buyer only trades when the value is 70, but the noise edge is small. Pushing the ask up to about 68 gives the best result.
- **Bid:** a bid around 46 maximises the expected edge.

{"bid": 46, "ask": 68}

Fair value after the sell is about **51.3** (contract value 10 × heads).

**Fair value before the trade**
- After three heads, the chance the coin is the 0.7 coin rises from 0.6 to about 0.80.
- That puts the probability of heads on each remaining flip at about 0.661.
- Expected total heads is 3 + 4 × 0.661 ≈ 5.64, so fair value was about 56.4.

**Effect of the sell at 46**
- An informed trader only sells at 46 if the final value is 40 or less. That means at most 1 head in the last 4 flips. This has prior probability of about 0.128.
- A noise trader sells at 46 with probability about 0.17.
- Updating on the sell drops expected remaining heads from 2.64 to about 2.13.

**Settlement distribution given the sell**

| Settlement value | 30 | 40 | 50 | 60 | 70 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 0.055 | 0.323 | 0.204 | 0.271 | 0.147 |

**Choosing the quotes**
- **Bid at 40:** an informed trader only sells into it when the value is 30. Noise sellers still hit it often enough to earn about +0.9 per quote in expectation.
- **Ask at 62:** this sits above the 60 outcome, so only the 70 outcome lets informed buyers profit. The expected edge is about +0.7, near the best of the asks tested.
- Being long 1 is well within the ±5 limit, so it doesn't change the quotes.

{"bid": 40, "ask": 62}

Four heads have been revealed, so the coin is now much more likely to be the 0.7 coin, and the fair value is about 60.1. Trading history adds little information.

**Posterior on the coin**
- Chance of seeing 4 heads with the 0.5 coin: 0.0625. Weighted by its prior of 0.4, that gives 0.025.
- Chance of seeing 4 heads with the 0.7 coin: 0.2401. Weighted by its prior of 0.6, that gives 0.144.
- So P(0.7 coin) ≈ 0.852 and P(0.5 coin) ≈ 0.148.
- The expected chance of heads on each remaining flip is about 0.670.

**Settlement value**
- With 3 flips left, the fair value is 40 + 30 × 0.670 ≈ 60.1.

| Settlement | Probability |
|---|---|
| 40 | 0.04 |
| 50 | 0.22 |
| 60 | 0.43 |
| 70 | 0.31 |

**Choosing the quotes**
- **Ask:** If the ask is between 60 and 70, informed traders buy whenever the value is 70. An ask of 70 removes that loss while still capturing noise buyers. Its expected profit is about 1.18, the best of the asks I tried.
- **Bid:** A bid just under 50 is only hit by informed traders when the value is 40, which has a probability of only 0.04. Its expected profit is about 1.03, the best of the bids I tried.

{"bid": 49.9, "ask": 70}

I'm quoting 52 / 70.1, wide around a fair value of about 62.

game.title: Coin of unknown bias
game.description: A coin is picked at random from a set of coins: P(heads) = 0.5 with probability 7/10, P(heads) = 0.7 with probability 3/10. The coin is not shown. It is flipped 6 times. Revealed flips show 1 for heads and 0 for tails.
game.contract: The contract settles at 5 times the number of heads in all flips.

info.raw:
Before any reveal, the expected value is about 16.8. That is 5 × 6 flips × 0.56, where 0.56 = 0.7·0.5 + 0.3·0.7 is the average chance of heads. The standard deviation is about 6.6.

Informed traders' valuations can only be multiples of 5, so I place my quotes just inside 10 and 25:

- **Ask at 24.9:** informed traders buy only when the value is 25 or 30 (about a 20% chance), and each such trade costs me only about 1 per unit. Noise traders above 24.9 still buy, so on average I gain about 0.7 per quote on this side.
- **Bid at 9.9:** informed traders sell only when the value is 0 or 5 (about an 8% chance). Noise traders below 9.9 still sell, so on average I gain about 0.6 per quote on this side.

Moving either quote inside the next multiple of 5 does worse. At an ask of 19.9, for example, informed traders would also buy whenever the value is 20, which is likely enough to make that side lose money.

{"bid": 9.9, "ask": 24.9}

I'm repeating last quote's prices: 9.9 bid and 24.9 ask. Both sides still look profitable.

**Fair value.** The coin is fair with probability 0.7 and has P(heads) = 0.7 with probability 0.3. That gives an average P(heads) of 0.56, so expected heads over 6 flips is 3.36. The prior fair value is 5 × 3.36 = 16.8.

**Update from quote 1.** The 9.9 / 24.9 quote drew no trade. That is more likely if the true value is 10, 15 or 20. Updating on this moves the expected number of heads to about 3.22, so fair value is now about 16.1.

**Why the bid stays at 9.9.**
- An informed trader would only sell to me if the value is 5 or 0. Those outcomes are now about 3.5% likely in total.
- A noise trader sells about 27% of the time, and on average I gain about 6.2 per trade.
- The expected profit is about +0.73. Bidding 14.9 instead would lose money, because informed traders would also sell whenever the value is 10.

**Why the ask stays at 24.9.**
- An informed trader would only buy if the value is 30, which is about 2% likely.
- A noise trader buys about 19% of the time, gaining me about 8.8 per trade.
- The expected profit is about +0.77. That beats asking 20.1 (about +0.42) or 29.9 (about +0.57).

{"bid": 9.9, "ask": 24.9}

Quoting **9.9 bid / 24.9 ask** again. The two earlier quotes at these prices got no trades, so the public fair value is still about 16.8.

**Fair value with nothing revealed**
- The chance of heads averages 0.7·0.5 + 0.3·0.7 = 0.56.
- Over 6 flips that is 3.36 expected heads, so the contract is worth 16.8.

**Settlement distribution.** The contract can settle at 0, 5, …, 30 with these probabilities:

| Settlement | 0 | 5 | 10 | 15 | 20 | 25 | 30 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 0.011 | 0.069 | 0.182 | 0.274 | 0.261 | 0.156 | 0.046 |

**Choosing the ask**
- At 24.9, an informed trader buys only when the settlement is 25 or 30. That costs about 0.13 per quote.
- A noise trader buys about 21% of the time and I make 8.1 each time, worth about +0.84.
- Net is about +0.71 per quote. A lower ask such as 22 nets about +0.36, and 20.1 is roughly breakeven. A higher ask of 29.9 nets about +0.61, so 24.9 is the best.

**Choosing the bid**
- At 9.9, an informed trader sells only when the settlement is 0 or 5. That costs about 0.22 per quote.
- Noise traders sell to me often enough to bring in about +0.84.
- Net is about +0.61. Bidding 5.1 gives a similar result (about +0.67), while 14.9 loses money.

{"bid": 9.9, "ask": 24.9}

Fair value is about 19.0–19.4. I quote wide on both sides, at bid 10.0 and ask 28.0, because each side then gives up money to the informed trader only in an unlikely extreme outcome.

**Fair value**
- Flip 1 came up heads, which shifts belief toward the 0.7 coin: P(p=0.7) = 0.21 / 0.56 = 0.375.
- The expected heads rate is then 0.575.
- Expected value is 5 × (1 + 5 × 0.575) = **19.375**.
- The stage‑1 trading (two no‑trades, then a buy at 24.9) moves this only slightly down, to about **19.0**. The no‑trades point to a middling outcome and roughly offset the buy.

**Ask side**
- For an ask between 25 and 30, the informed trader buys only if the settlement value is 30 (all five remaining flips heads, about 7% likely). That costs about 0.1–0.2 per quote.
- Noise traders still lift an ask in the 27–29 range often enough to earn about 0.75 expected per quote. That beats an ask just below 25 (about 0.63), where the informed trader also buys at a value of 25.

**Bid side**
- For a bid between 5 and 10, the informed trader sells only if the value is 5 (all remaining flips tails, about 0.3% likely).
- A bid of about 10 earns about 0.8 expected from noise sellers. Bids in the 12–15 range invite informed selling at values of 10 and 15 and do worse.

**Position**
- I am short 1, which is small, so I don't skew the quotes.

{"bid": 10.0, "ask": 28.0}

Fair value works out to about 18.6.

**How I got there**
- Flip 1 came up heads. That raises the chance we have the 0.7 coin from 30% to 37.5%.
- I then weighed the trading history against each possible total of heads:
  - Quotes 1 and 2 had no trades. That makes very low and very high totals less likely.
  - Quote 3 was a buy at 24.9. That favours a total of 5 or more heads.
  - Quote 4 had no trade at 10 / 28.
- The resulting chances for the total number of heads (H) are:
  - H ≤ 2: about 13%
  - H = 3: about 28%
  - H = 4: about 36%
  - H = 5: about 20%
  - H = 6: about 3%
- That gives an expected 3.72 heads, so fair value ≈ 18.6.

**Setting the quote**
- The settlement value is always a multiple of 5. So a bid just above 10 and an ask just above 25 lose almost nothing to an informed trader.
- An informed trader only takes the ask if the value is 30, which has about a 3% chance.
- They only hit the bid if the value is 10 or below, and at 10.1 that costs at most a few tenths per trade on average.
- Noise traders still trade often enough at these prices to make each side profitable on average.

{"bid": 10.1, "ask": 25.1}

Fair value is about 19.1, after updating on flip 1 = 1 and on what the trades so far reveal:

- **From flip 1 alone:** the 0.7-bias coin has posterior 0.375. Expected heads are 1 + 5 × 0.575 = 3.875, so the value is 19.4.
- **From the trading history:** the buy at 24.9 suggests a high value. The no-trades at quotes 4 and 5 rule out very high and very low outcomes. Taken together, these bring the fair value to about 19.1.
- **Possible settlements:** the contract can only settle at multiples of 5. The posterior is roughly 5% at 10, 32% at 15, 40% at 20, 22% at 25 and 1% at 30.

**Ask:** 24.9 sits just below 25. An informed buyer only costs me 0.1 when the value is 25, which is unlikely, and only loses me real money if it is 30. Noise traders still buy fairly often, at about 5.8 above fair. Expected value is about +0.77 per quote.

**Bid:** around 12 is best. An informed seller only arrives if the value is 10, and then I lose just 2. Noise sellers trade often enough at about 7 below fair. Expected value is about +0.79. A bid near 12 also helps me cover my short position.

{"bid": 12, "ask": 24.9}

The fair value is about 15.46, and I'm quoting outside the informed trader's possible values: bid 8.0, ask 23.0.

**Which coin it is.** Revealed flips show 2 heads in 4.
- Likelihood under the fair coin: 0.5⁴ = 0.0625. Times its prior of 0.7, that gives 0.04375.
- Likelihood under the biased coin: 0.7² × 0.3² = 0.0441. Times its prior of 0.3, that gives 0.01323.
- So the probability the coin is biased (P(heads) = 0.7) is about 0.232.
- I ignored the stage‑1 buy at 24.9, which would only nudge this slightly higher.

**Settlement value.** It is 5 × (2 + H), where H is heads in flips 5 and 6.

| H | Settlement | Probability |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 10 | ≈ 0.213 |
| 1 | 15 | ≈ 0.481 |
| 2 | 20 | ≈ 0.306 |

Expected value is about 15.46.

**Choice of quotes.** The informed trader's valuation is exactly 10, 15 or 20. If my ask is above 20 and my bid is below 10, an informed trader never trades with me. I only meet noise traders, whose valuations centre on 15.46 with standard deviation 9.9.

The expected edge per quote is 0.5 × P(trade) × distance from fair:
- An ask around 23 maximises this, at about 0.84.
- A bid around 8 does the same, at about 0.84.
- An ask just under 20 (at 19.9) does worse, about 0.71, because the informed trader buys whenever the value is 20.

{"bid": 8.0, "ask": 23.0}

The fair value is about 15.5, so I'm quoting wide: bid 8.4, ask 22.9.

**Coin posterior.** The revealed flips show 2 heads in 4.
- Likelihood if the coin is fair: 0.5⁴ = 0.0625.
- Likelihood if the coin is biased (0.7): 0.7²·0.3² = 0.0441.
- With the 7/10 and 3/10 priors, P(biased coin | flips) = 0.01323 / 0.05698 ≈ 0.232.
- So the chance of heads on each of flips 5 and 6 is 0.5 + 0.2·0.232 ≈ 0.546.

**Settlement distribution.** Two flips are left, so the contract settles at 10, 15 or 20.
- P(10) ≈ 0.213
- P(15) ≈ 0.481
- P(20) ≈ 0.306
- Fair value ≈ 5·(2 + 1.093) ≈ 15.46.

**Ask.** If the ask is at or above 20, informed traders never buy, because their valuation is at most 20. Profit then comes only from noise traders, whose valuations are roughly N(15.46, 9.9). I want to maximise P(noise valuation > ask) × (ask − 15.46).
- At an ask of 22: 0.255 × 6.5 ≈ 1.67.
- At an ask of 23: 0.223 × 7.5 ≈ 1.68.
- At an ask of 24: about 1.66.
- The curve is flat near 23, so I'll ask about 22.9.

**Bid.** Symmetrically, if the bid is at or below 10, informed traders never sell to me. I want to maximise P(noise valuation < bid) × (15.46 − bid).
- At a bid of 8: 0.225 × 7.46 ≈ 1.68.
- At a bid of 9: about 1.66.
- So I'll bid about 8.4.

**Position.** I'm at −1 with two quotes left, so the ±5 limit can't bind.

{"bid": 8.4, "ask": 22.9}

With 2 heads in the 4 revealed flips, the fair value is about 15.5, and a wide quote of 8.0 / 22.9 maximises expected profit.

**Which coin is it?**
- Fair coin: likelihood of these flips is 0.5⁴ = 0.0625.
- Biased coin (0.7 heads): likelihood is 0.7²·0.3² = 0.0441.
- Posterior that the coin is biased is 0.3·0.0441 / (0.3·0.0441 + 0.7·0.0625) ≈ 0.232.

**Fair value**
- Expected P(heads) is 0.5 + 0.2·0.232 ≈ 0.546.
- Expected heads in the last two flips is 2 · 0.546 ≈ 1.09.
- Fair value is 5 · (2 + 1.09) ≈ 15.46.

**Settlement outcomes**

| Settlement value | Probability |
|---|---|
| 10 | ≈ 0.213 |
| 15 | ≈ 0.481 |
| 20 | ≈ 0.306 |

**Ask**
- Any ask below 20 loses money to informed buyers when the value is 20.
- Above 20, only noise traders buy, at fair value plus Normal noise with standard deviation 9.9.
- Expected profit from them is (ask − 15.46) × P(valuation > ask). This peaks at about 0.75 standard deviations above fair value, an ask of about 22.9.
- At 22.9 the expected profit is about 0.84, against about 0.74 at an ask of 20.1.

**Bid**
- By the same logic, a bid above 10 loses money to informed sellers when the value is 10.
- Below 10, only noise traders sell. The best bid is about 15.46 − 7.4 ≈ 8.0.
- At 8.0 the expected profit is about 0.84, against about 0.79 at a bid of 10.

{"bid": 8.0, "ask": 22.9}
